```
GPU 0 has a total capacity of 267.68 GiB of which 26.77 GiB is free. Including
non-PyTorch memory, this process has 240.52 GiB memory in use. Of the allocated
memory 235.23 GiB is allocated by PyTorch, with 5.54 GiB allocated in private
pools (e.g., CUDA Graphs), and 1.43 GiB is reserved by PyTorch but unallocated.
```

Both TP ranks hit the same error at the same time. The scheduler raises, and the whole server process exits (`kill_process_tree`). Every in-flight request drops. A second replica took over the failover traffic and hit the same crash 12 minutes later, at a smaller allocation size (15.40 GiB tried, 12.74 GiB free). So this is not a one-off. It reproduces whenever the queue depth and context length are large enough compared to whatever memory happens to be free at the time.

Traceback (identical shape on both occurrences, both ranks):
```
Scheduler hit an exception: Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py", line 5696, in run_scheduler_process
    scheduler.run_event_loop()
  File "sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py", line 1839, in run_event_loop
    ... dispatch_event_loop -> forward
  File "sglang/srt/layers/attention/deepseek_v4_backend.py", line 3904, in _forward_prefill_sparse
    workspace = self.sparse_prefill_workspace.get(
                ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "sglang/srt/layers/attention/dsv4/sparse_prefill_utils.py", line 100, in get
    self._buffer = torch.empty(
                   ^^^^^^^^^^^^
torch.OutOfMemoryError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 27.20 GiB. ...
```

Batch state at the moment of the first crash: `#running-req: 0, #queue-req: 73, #pending-token: 337719` (a 73-request queue draining at once). Second occurrence: `#running-req: 4, #queue-req: 16, #pending-token: 388518`.

**Analysis.** `SparsePrefillWorkspace.get()` in `sparse_prefill_utils.py` reallocates its buffer with a plain `torch.empty(...)` call whenever the requested size is bigger than the current buffer. There is no check before this call:

```python
def get(self, num_tokens, dtype=torch.bfloat16):
    assert num_tokens > 0
    current_capacity = self._buffer.shape[0] if self._buffer is not None else 0
    current_dtype = self._buffer.dtype if self._buffer is not None else None
    if num_tokens > current_capacity or dtype != current_dtype:
        self._buffer = torch.empty(
            (num_tokens, 1, WORKSPACE_DIM), dtype=dtype, device=self.device,
        )
    return self._buffer[:num_tokens]
```

It is called from `_forward_prefill_sparse` with `num_tokens = n_compressed + cache.swa_token_ids.shape[0]`. That is the size of the compressed-region gather plus the SWA-region gather for every request in that prefill step. There is no `mem_get_info` check and no chunking anywhere in this path.

This is not bounded by `--max-prefill-tokens`. That flag only caps new tokens admitted per step. The crashing batch shows `#new-token: 16384`, right at that cap, so the throttle was respected and it still was not enough. It is also not bounded by `--chunked-prefill-size`. Grepping the file shows this flag is never read or enforced against this workspace. So a deep queue of long-context requests can push `n_compressed + swa_token_ids` well past what the new-token cap limits, and the allocation just tries for whatever that adds up to. There is no fallback.

This looks like the same bug class as #30505 (unbudgeted prefill transients in DSA's `flash_mla_with_kvcache` on GLM-5.2) and the budget-check gap we already fixed in the DSV4 indexer's MQA-logits path (related to #34155 and #33246). But this is a different call site, `SparsePrefillWorkspace`, and it has no budget or chunking guard at all.

**Suggestion.** Add the same kind of guard used for the DSV4 indexer's MQA-logits budget check. Read `torch.cuda.mem_get_info()` before the `torch.empty(...)` call in `SparsePrefillWorkspace.get()`. Then either chunk the prefill batch to fit, or raise an error that can be retried, instead of letting an oversized allocation take down the whole TP group. A single request failing is a much better outcome than the whole server crashing on one bad batch.

title: [Feature][DeepSeek-V4.1] Decode graph width is pinned to --context-length; add a decode-phase max_seq_len
body:
### TL;DR

On SM90, `--context-length` sets the decode indexer's **scan width**, not only the maximum servable context. The decode CUDA graph is captured with `max_seq_len = MAX_SEQ_LEN_FOR_CAPTURE = req_to_token.shape[1]`, and `PagedIndexerMetadata.max_compressed_seq_len` derives the indexer kernel's fixed column count from it. A deployment that actually serves 2K-token contexts therefore pays for a 1M-token scan on every decode step.

Measured, that is a **2.68x decode lever** — and it is not escapable from config: `PhaseConfig.max_seq_len` is accepted for `Phase.PREFILL` but not for `Phase.DECODE`, so the only way to collect it is to lower `--context-length` and give up long context.

PRs #39046 / #40431 / #40176 reduce the *work* done per capacity-sized tile, but they explicitly preserve the launch grid and the graph width. This is the complementary knob: let the decode graph be captured narrow, and fall back to eager for live contexts that exceed it — mirroring what prefill already does via `max_context_size` + `can_run_prefill_cuda_graph`.

### Environment

- 8 x H200, SM90 (sm_90), driver 570.211.01 / CUDA 12.8, all-to-all NV18
- `lmsysorg/sglang:dev-cu12-dsv41` @ `824bb45e1bf7486e49034bfa4bcad59aba799540`
- DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (FP8 checkpoint; an md5-identical-config drop-in variant)
- `--tp-size 4 --ep-size 4 --context-length 1048576 --max-running-requests 8 --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 8 --chunked-prefill-size 8192 --mem-fraction-static 0.70 --schedule-policy lpm --moe-runner-backend humming --speculative-algorithm DSPARK --speculative-dspark-block-size 4 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 5`
- Replica B only; replica A's container id and `StartedAt` asserted unchanged across every recreate

### Measurement

Decode tok/s **per request**, median of 5 repeats, one unmeasured warm round. Per-request (not aggregate) so batch effects are removed.

| `--context-length` | indexer capacity (cols) | 2048 x1 | 2048 x8 | 65536 x8 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **1048576** (baseline) | 262144 | 98.4 | **32.1** | 35.31 |
| 524288 | 131072 | 128.01 | 49.41 | 52.55 |
| 262144 | 65536 | 131.51 | 67.93 | 73.59 |
| 131072 | 32768 | **147.93** | **85.98** | **88.0** |
| **gain, 1M -> 128K** | | **1.50x** | **2.68x** | **2.49x** |

Adjacent-tier 5-repeat ranges are disjoint everywhere (e.g. 65536 x8: `33.81-35.92`, `52.38-53.82`, `70.98-75.21`, `85.02-92.99`), against a measured run-to-run spread of 10-13%.

Cell labels are nominal: the harness over-calibrated and real prompt lengths are 2658 / 84261 tokens. Prompt construction is byte-identical across tiers and variants, so the overshoot is common mode and does not bias the deltas.

Three things identify the mechanism as a per-row fixed-width scan rather than a length- or weight-proportional cost:

1. **bs=1 gains 50% and saturates; bs=8 gains 168% and is still climbing.** The same capacity reduction is worth 8x more in absolute terms at bs=8 while the step it is charged against grows far more slowly.
2. **Cost is linear in capacity.** Inverting to step time at n=8: 31.15 / 20.24 / 14.72 ms for 262144 / 131072 / 65536 columns — halving the capacity halves the saving (10.91 : 5.52 = 1.98).
3. **A registered prediction.** Fitting `step_time(n=8) = 9.27 ms + 83.2 ns * capacity_columns` predicted ~83 tok/s at the 131072 tier before that tier was run; measured **85.98**.

Service-level effect: aggregate wall-clock throughput at 2048 x8 moves 226-247 -> 347-369 tok/s at the first tier alone (+50%), with TTFT flat to noise (0.438 -> 0.442 s) and the KV pool unchanged (-0.67% once, then flat).

Fresh-boot control excludes allocator/JIT state: after restoring the 1M config on a freshly booted replica the identical probe reproduces the baseline (102.7 / 32.16 / 35.6).

### Source (main)

- `python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/dsv4/metadata.py:322-324` — `max_compressed_seq_len` = `page_table.shape[1] * compressed_page_size`
- `python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/dsv4/indexer.py:1067` — that value is handed to the decode indexer as a fixed argument
- `python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/deepseek_v4_backend.py:1214` — `MAX_SEQ_LEN_FOR_CAPTURE = self.req_to_token.shape[1]`; used for decode capture at `:2272-2298`
- `python/sglang/srt/model_executor/cuda_graph_config.py:78-88` — `ALLOWED_KEYS_PER_PHASE[Phase.DECODE]` has no `max_seq_len`; `Phase.PREFILL` has it (plus `max_context_size`)
- prefill already has the fallback this request wants for decode: `deepseek_v4_backend.py:1557-1559` (cap `num_pages` by the graph width) and `:1586-1592` (`can_run_prefill_cuda_graph`)

### Negative control

The identical `--max-model-len` change on vLLM, same box, same checkpoint, moves aggregate throughput by 3.6-4.9% (2048 x8: 1102.8 -> 1142.5; 65536 x8: 829.2 -> 869.9). vLLM's static launch shape with a per-row `[start, end)` loop has no such coupling, which rules out "this is the unavoidable price of sparse attention at 1M".

### What the lever costs today

Against 12h of production traffic, `--context-length=262144` rejects at most 1 request in 5005 (`#cached-token` p99.9 = 199,936 tokens, a 31% margin) while more than doubling decode at the concurrency production actually runs at. But 131072 is another 27% on top and cuts below p99.9 — a capability decision — and 1M becomes unreachable either way.

### Proposal

1. accept `"max_seq_len"` in `ALLOWED_KEYS_PER_PHASE[Phase.DECODE]`;
2. use it as `max_seq_len` for decode graph capture and decode metadata in place of `MAX_SEQ_LEN_FOR_CAPTURE`;
3. replay a decode batch eagerly when its live max sequence length exceeds it (mirror `can_run_prefill_cuda_graph`).

One caveat worth stating up front: the capture width cannot vary per batch, so a naive clamp inside the kernel would be *worse* than the flag — a clamped graph would silently ignore the tail of a longer sequence instead of rejecting it. A decode-only `max_seq_len` needs the same explicit eager fallback prefill has.

### Ask

Is this the intended direction, or is the plan to let #40431 / #40176 absorb the coupling at the kernel level? If the former, I am happy to prototype the config plumbing.

---

*Independent of #40431: that PR makes invisible tiles cheap while keeping the grid; this changes how many tiles exist and lets a 1M-context deployment capture a 128K decode graph.*

title: [Feature][Spec][XPU] Honor rejection sampling in EAGLE chain verification
body:
### Checklist

- [x] If this is not a feature request but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Motivation

EAGLE verification on XPU takes the greedy argmax path even when the batch is non-greedy and --speculative-use-rejection-sampling is enabled. For a configuration that passes the startup checks, the startup hook reports rejection sampling as enabled, but the XPU verification gate still prevents that sampler from being reached.

I would like to enable the existing chain-rejection path on XPU, subject to hardware validation and coordination with related work.

Current behavior

Source snapshot: 32290dda2cea4bb95274b3d08e43d4dad74e9676.

In python/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_utils.py, _verify_uses_greedy() returns:

return is_all_greedy or is_cpu or is_xpu or (
    is_hip and not use_rejection_sampling
)

The unconditional is_xpu term selects the branch containing torch.argmax(next_token_logits, dim=-1), including when is_all_greedy=False and use_rejection_sampling=True.

Meanwhile, speculative_hook.py logs:

Rejection sampling is enabled for speculative decoding (speculative_use_rejection_sampling=True).

The issue is therefore a mismatch between the enabled configuration and the verification path actually selected.

This is a source-level finding. I have not yet reproduced the behavior or validated an alternative on XPU hardware. The ignored flag was also noted as a side issue in #35144.

Proposed scope

Allow non-greedy XPU batches with rejection sampling explicitly enabled to reach chain_speculative_sampling_triton.

The existing startup checks and sampling-branch validation would remain unchanged:

The resolved algorithm must be EAGLE or EAGLE3, including NEXTN configurations that resolve to EAGLE.

--speculative-eagle-topk must be 1.

Both acceptance thresholds must be 1.0, and deterministic inference must be disabled.

Draft proposal probabilities must be present and use the target vocabulary.

These are inherited requirements of the existing rejection-sampling path, not additional XPU-specific restrictions. The speculative branching factor is separate from request-level sampling top_k.

Automatic enablement and the separate target-only stochastic tree-verification path are outside this proposal. Greedy requests and other backends should retain their existing behavior.

Related implementation work

#37134 provides a reference for enabling the Triton chain-rejection path on ROCm.

intel/llm-scaler#719, merged September 17, 2026, implements out-of-tree target-only stochastic XPU verification using SYCL/PyTorch operations and a patch to eagle_info_v2.py. It addresses the broader XPU sampling limitation, but is distinct from enabling the existing Triton chain sampler with actual draft proposal probabilities.

#34140 is also related to the separate target-only tree path on ROCm. I would like to coordinate with these efforts rather than duplicate planned upstream work.

Implementation considerations

Once XPU reaches the rejection-sampling branch, the existing renormalization dispatch already imports top_k_renorm_prob and top_p_renorm_prob from sgl_kernel.

The XPU dependency file pins sglang-kernel-xpu 0.2.0. I would first verify that this pinned wheel exposes working versions of the required operations and validate their cutoff and tie semantics against the intended sampling behavior. Related XPU sampler integration: #38510.

The Triton/PyTorch renormalization fallback is an alternative, not the existing XPU route. Using it would require explicit dispatch changes and an XPU-compatible _prepare_probs guard.

The sampling branch also broadcasts verification results across tensor-parallel ranks. TP > 1 therefore needs explicit validation in light of #35144/#35195; enabling the gate alone would not establish multi-XPU correctness.

Validation

Validation should include:

Gate-routing and configuration regression tests, including unchanged greedy behavior and the existing unsupported-configuration checks.

Actual XPU chain-sampler and renormalization tests against independent references, covering acceptance, rejection, all-drafts-accepted sampling, and top-k/top-p boundary and tie cases.

End-to-end non-greedy and mixed greedy/non-greedy batches, with distributional checks rather than output diversity or task accuracy alone.

Graph capture enabled/disabled and TP=1/TP>1 where supported, preserving and testing the existing draft_probs copy after graph replay so the proposal probabilities remain intact until verification.

Maintainer input

Is there an upstreaming plan for intel/llm-scaler#719 or another XPU verification effort that this should coordinate with? Would a focused in-tree chain-rejection enablement PR be useful alongside the target-only work?

I do not currently have guaranteed XPU hardware access. Before committing to an implementation, I would appreciate guidance on the preferred approach and whether hardware validation could be coordinated with an XPU contributor.

### Related resources

_No response_

title: [Bug] DFLASH draft layout is assumed, not validated: anchor-first checkpoints shift every position silently
body:
# [Bug] DFLASH draft layout is assumed, not validated: anchor-first checkpoints shift every position silently

### Summary

`DFLASH` draft checkpoints carry an implicit block-layout convention, and SGLang assumes
one of the two conventions in common use without checking which one a checkpoint was
trained with. A checkpoint trained with the *anchor-as-first-prediction* layout — where
every position in the block predicts — is served without any error and produces draft
tokens shifted by one position. The server reports healthy; acceptance collapses to
roughly `1.0` (only the anchor/bonus token survives).

Isolated on a Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (`Qwen4Exp`) target with the official DeepSpec drafter
`dflash_block7_qwen38_flash_next` on 8×A800 (SM80): **accept length @ 4-token window =
1.0621** over 47,411 verify steps. The same checkpoint's card reports a *served* accepted
length of **2.7562 at block 4** and **2.9837 at its native block 7** under vLLM, where the
layout it was trained for is honoured. No warning, no assertion here — the service starts
and answers normally, at a fraction of that acceptance.

### The two conventions

| | anchor-as-first-prediction | 1+N (SGLang's assumption) |
|---|---|---|
| block positions | all `K` positions predict | position 0 is the seeded anchor/bonus token; positions `1..N` are the drafts |
| marker, when present | `sample_from_anchor: true` | `sample_from_anchor: false` |
| drafter | DeepSpec `dflash_block7_qwen38_flash_next` | speculators-format drafts |

The marker is a **speculators** config field (`DFlashSpeculatorConfig.sample_from_anchor`,
default `False`; `DSparkSpeculatorConfig` defaults `True`). The convention also determines the
token count: `False` → `block_size - 1` speculative tokens, `True` → `block_size`.

**It is not a reliable discriminator across the ecosystem, which is part of the problem.**
The official anchor-first checkpoint above carries **no `sample_from_anchor` field at all** —
neither top-level nor inside its `dflash_config`; its config exposes `num_anchors: 512` and
nothing else about the layout. So a marker-based check would read the sglang default and wave
exactly the checkpoint that mis-serves through.

**But the layout *is* declared — under a name SGLang does not read.** The upstream serving repo
ships a config override (the README notes the checkpoint's own `config.json` "does not carry the
`dflash_config` block the engine reads"). That override's `dflash_config` contains:

```json
"dflash_config": {
  "target_layer_ids": [3, 15, 23, 35, 43],
  "mask_token_id": 248077,
  "use_aux_hidden_state": true,
  "causal": false,
  "query_zero_predicts_next": true
}
```

`query_zero_predicts_next: true` is a direct, explicit statement of the anchor-first convention.
SGLang's `DFlashDraftConfig` (`speculative/dflash_utils.py:529-548`) has no field for it and
`parse_dflash_draft_config` never reads it — a tree-wide search for the identifier returns zero
hits. So the declaration exists, is unambiguous, and is silently dropped.

> **Inference, not a confirmed contract.** I am reading `query_zero_predicts_next` as "the
> query at position 0 predicts the token *after* the anchor", i.e. the anchor-first layout —
> that is what the field name says and it is consistent with the extra `block_size`-th
> prediction the layout implies, but I have not verified it against the trainer source and am
> labelling it as a hypothesis rather than a spec. If the maintainers confirm the field's
> meaning, a check on it is the natural fix; if not, the layout still has to be established
> some other way. It should not be shipped as a hard gate on my reading alone.

### Where SGLang assumes 1+N

`DFlashWorkerV2` slices the draft's hidden states to drop position 0:

```python
# python/sglang/srt/speculative/dflash_worker_v2.py:158-160
# draft tokens are block positions 1: (pos 0 is the seeded bonus token)
bs = hidden_states.shape[0] // self.block_size
hs = hidden_states.view(bs, self.block_size, -1)[:, 1:, :].reshape(
    -1, hidden_states.shape[-1]
)
```

The same slice appears in the in-worker draft path (`dflash_worker_v2.py:278`,
`# pos 0 = anchor`) and in the selector path (`:1378`, `:2572`).

A checkpoint trained anchor-first produces `K` meaningful predictions per block, but only
`K-1` of them are read, and each one is read from the *wrong* slot — a uniform off-by-one
across every draft position.

### The layout field is already parsed — just not for this

`dflash_utils.py` already reads `sample_from_anchor` off the draft config:

```python
# python/sglang/srt/speculative/dflash_utils.py:504-507
sample_from_anchor = dflash_config.get(
    "sample_from_anchor", _cfg_get(config, "sample_from_anchor", True)
)
return sample_from_anchor is False
```

Two things follow from that snippet. First, the field is already parsed at config-parse time.
Second, **its default is inverted for this purpose**: `_cfg_get(..., True)` reads the sglang
default as `True`, but the speculators default for the DFlash family is `False`. So "absent"
means *opposite* things to the two sides, which is why absence cannot be treated as safety.

Today the read is confined to `is_nemotron_35_draft_config` (`dflash_utils.py:470`), and even
there it is one of six conjunctive conditions identifying one specific published checkpoint —
it is not a general layout gate. The value is available on the DFLASH path and simply not
consulted there.

### Suggested fix (fail fast, matching vLLM)

vLLM's DFlash speculator raises on this exact layout
(`ValueError: sample_from_anchor=True is not supported for DFlash`). SGLang currently does
something worse than raising: it serves, silently, at ~1.0 acceptance.

Three options, in increasing order of how much they depend on my unverified reading above:

1. **Minimal, no inference needed for the check itself:** fail fast on the checkpoints that *do*
   declare a layout — anything SGLang can currently see (`sample_from_anchor` where present).
   Wiring up `query_zero_predicts_next` would extend this to the official checkpoint, but **that
   rests on my unverified reading of the field (hypothesis, see above) — it should only be
   treated as a gate once the semantics are confirmed.** As it stands this option would not have
   caught the official checkpoint, because SGLang reads neither field today; it is a strict
   improvement over the current state and commits to nothing uncertain.
2. **Require an explicit declaration** on the DFLASH draft config going forward, and refuse to
   serve a checkpoint that omits it. Catches everything, including this checkpoint — at the
   cost of breaking checkpoints that are in the wild today.
3. **Honour the layout** — read all `K` positions when the checkpoint is anchor-first. The most
   useful outcome, and a bounded change at the four slice sites above, but it is downstream of
   the layout actually being established.

Either way the checkpoint stops being served at a wrong-but-plausible acceptance rate.

The design constraint worth flagging: **an explicit check on `sample_from_anchor` alone would
not have caught this checkpoint** — it declares neither that field nor `speculative_tokens`
(the identifier does not appear anywhere in its config). Whatever is chosen has to *establish*
the layout rather than default it.

Two things I'd be glad to be corrected on: whether `query_zero_predicts_next` means what I read
it to mean, and whether there is a better discriminator for layout than anything proposed here
— I've only looked at one checkpoint family and would rather defer to the maintainers than guess.

### Reproduction

**Prerequisite:** this needs the Qwen4-Exp capture guard from **#38642** (rebased onto current
main). On bare main the Qwen4-Exp DFLASH path never reaches the draft at all — the server dies
during decode CUDA-graph capture (`ValueError: too many values to unpack (expected 2)`, see
#38589). With the guard, the server comes up and the numbers below reproduce.

SM80 (8×A800), main + #38642, official DeepSpec drafter, `--speculative-num-draft-tokens 4`:

```bash
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path <Qwen3.8-Flash-Next target> \
  --speculative-algorithm DFLASH \
  --speculative-draft-model-path <DFlash2 draft, block 4, 24 heads, taps [1,7,14,20,26,32,39,45]> \
  --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 --tp 8 \
  --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 8 --mem-fraction-static 0.85
```
(8xA800 SM80, driver 550.144.03, torch 2.11.0+cu130. On SM80 the tilelang/nvcc header
check also needs `NVCC_PREPEND_FLAGS=-DCCCL_DISABLE_CTK_COMPATIBILITY_CHECK`.)

Note that `--speculative-num-draft-tokens 4` is not a free choice here: Qwen4-Exp's QSA
caps the window at its compression ratio
(`layers/attention/qwen_sparse_attn_backend.py:240`, `_require_chain_speculation`), so a
`block_size=7` checkpoint cannot even be launched at its training block size.

### Measured acceptance (4-token window)

| concurrency | requests | failures | accept length | accept rate |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 8 | 300 | 0 | **1.0621** | 0.0184 |
| 24 | 300 | 0 | 1.0643 | 0.0190 |
| 48 | 300 | 0 | 1.0629 | 0.0186 |

An earlier independent run at concurrency 8 gave 1.0604 (47,377 steps), i.e. run-to-run spread
at fixed concurrency is ~0.002.

Per-position, pooled over 47,411 verify steps (concurrency 8):

| position k | P(accept at k \| prefix matched) | P(accept length ≥ k) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0.0497 | 0.0497 |
| 2 | 0.1024 | 0.0051 |
| 3 | 0.3485 | 0.0018 |

95.0% of verify steps accept **zero** draft tokens; the bottleneck is position 1. The
6×-concurrency sweep moves accept length by <0.4%, so this is steady-state behaviour, not
a load artifact.

### Related

- #38589 — the sibling report on this target: Qwen4Exp cannot emit DFlash aux hidden
  states at all. That is a prerequisite failure; this one is what remains once a drafter
  *can* be served.
- Same shape of problem, one layer down: the block-size mismatch between a draft's training
  `block_size` and the served `--speculative-num-draft-tokens` is warned about
  (`dflash_worker_v2.py:468`) and then silently forced (`:472`). DFLASH's convolution
  indexes by `position % block_size`, so a mismatch shifts positions too. Fail-fast there
  would have caught this class of problem earlier.

Happy to test either fix on the SM80 rig.

title: [Roadmap] SGLang dLLM Serving
body:
# Goal

This roadmap continues #14199, initiated by @ClawSeven, and builds on the community's work toward robust, efficient block-diffusion serving and Jev-style decisions on diffusion LLMs.

Carry forward unfinished serving goals alongside newer work. Full-sequence models get baseline compatibility. Checked items record merged work. Unchecked items track remaining work or evaluation. Phases can overlap. Jev-style decisions on causal models are tracked separately, starting with #40826.

# Roadmap

### Phase 1: Shared runtime and request lifecycle

- [ ] Complete shared scheduling support.

  - [x] Dynamic batching. #14883
  - [x] Prefill/decode separation. #17484
  - [x] Algorithm-independent FDFO and early block departure. #27551
  - [ ] Refine scheduling interfaces and isolate model behavior.
  - [ ] FDFO + LowConfidence overlap scheduling. @Betelgeu #40756
  - [ ] Extend overlap to other algorithms after state-lifetime qualification.

- [ ] Harden request lifecycle and caching.

  - [x] Block-level radix caching. #18724
  - [x] Retain block KV and request slots. #27877
  - [ ] Qualify aborted FDFO cleanup and retained KV recovery.
  - [ ] Bound staging admission by block size and available capacity. #32992
  - [ ] Radix-cache ownership fix candidate. #35470
  - [ ] Cross-cache ownership fix candidate. #35781
  - [ ] Preserve literal mask text. #35998
  - [ ] Qualify committed streaming, EOS/stops, cancellation, and final assembly. @zxr-creator
  - [ ] Define opt-in provisional output separately from committed streaming.

### Phase 2: Prefill and CUDA graphs

- [ ] Expand attention and prefill support.

  - [ ] FlashInfer multi-block prefill and Breakable graphs. #31586

title: [Bug] Mooncake DFlash draft KV transfer fails with asymmetric P/D TP on GLM-5.3-Flash
body:
## Checklist
- [x] Searched related reports: #36140 covers missing DFlash PD state; #40045 handles heterogeneous draft-head slicing in the DCP path, not this non-DCP path.
- [x] Inspected current main at be495a6174. The non-DCP hybrid-MLA branch still calls send_kvcache, which passes the source item lengths to the generic transfer for both source and destination offsets.
- [ ] Full python3 -m sglang.check_env output from the original GPU run is not preserved.

## Describe the bug
With Mooncake PD disaggregation, GLM-5.3-Flash plus DFlash2 and smaller prefill TP than decode TP can fail KV transfer. Target MLA KV has compatible per-rank layout, but the draft KV is head-sharded: a P TP2 draft page has twice the per-rank bytes of a D TP4 draft page. The generic transfer uses the P item length as the D stride, so draft writes address the wrong D locations. This is a different path from the DCP-specific relayout merged in #40045.

## Reproduction
- Model: GLM-5.3-Flash with a compatible DFlash2 draft checkpoint (BF16 draft KV).
- Hardware: B300. Two P replicas, each TP2/EP2; one D worker TP4/EP4. No CP/DCP.
- Both roles: `--speculative-algorithm DFLASH --speculative-draft-model-path <draft> --speculative-dflash-block-size 8 --disaggregation-transfer-backend mooncake`. P uses `--disaggregation-mode prefill`; D uses `--disaggregation-mode decode`. CacheLink disabled.
- Route through Hydra; send 256 chat-completions requests at concurrency 64, with approximately 4096 input and 1536 output tokens.
- Observed before the local fix: 228/256 completed, with 28 failed KV transfers. Narrowing RDMA HCAs removed transport retries but did not remove these failures. A local prototype that keeps target KV on the generic path and transfers only the owning D rank draft-head slice completed 256/256 on the same short regression. This is transfer-completion evidence, not a full accuracy claim.

## Expected behavior
P TP2 to D TP4 should preserve each D rank draft KV head slice and use destination per-entry item lengths for destination addresses, without changing the target KV path. Unsupported layouts should fail explicitly rather than silently copy with the P stride.

## Environment
Original reproduction: B300, SGLang v0.5.19-based 2026-09-22 nightly image, Mooncake RDMA, DFlash2 block size 8. Code-path inspection above is against community main be495a6174 (2026-09-24); a full GPU rerun on this exact main commit remains pending.

title: [Bug] Prefill input logprobs are served from the wrong request when a batch member is retracted or finished
body:
### Describe the bug

In `process_batch_result_prefill`, the branch that skips finished-in-a-mixed-batch and retracted requests does not advance `logprob_pt`, so every later request in the same batch reads a shifted slice of the flat input-logprob array and is served **another request's prompt logprobs**.

The flat array holds one block per request in batch order regardless of whether that request asked for logprobs. That is why `_apply_prefill_logprobs` advances the cursor outside its `return_logprob` guard ([`batch_result_processor.py:522`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler_components/batch_result_processor.py#L522)):

```python
        if req.return_logprob:
            self.logprob_result_processor.add_logprob_return_values(...)
        logprob_pt += num_input_logprobs
        return logprob_pt
```

The producer agrees: `logits_processor.py` builds `extend_logprob_pruned_lens_cpu` by appending `extend_len - start_len` for every sequence in the batch, using the same formula the consumer uses in `calculate_num_input_logprobs`.

But the skip at [`batch_result_processor.py:307-313`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler_components/batch_result_processor.py#L307-L313) steps over a request without stepping the cursor:

```python
                if (
                    req.finished() and req.inflight_middle_chunks <= 0
                ) or req.is_retracted:
                    # Decode req in a mixed batch, or a retracted req. Keep an
                    # aborted middle chunk in the chunked branch long enough to
                    # drain its accounting without streaming it.
                    continue
```

`logprob_pt` is initialized at line 286 and advanced only at lines 344 and 374, both after this `continue`.

Nothing raises. The assertion in `logprob_result_processor.py` checks the slice **length**, not its offset, and the shift is always backwards, so it never runs off the end. The diagnostic signature is that `input_top_logprobs_val[i]` is indexed per request and stays correct while `input_token_logprobs` is sliced by the cursor and is wrong.

The disaggregated prefill loop already handles exactly this. `disaggregation/prefill.py:703` defines `advance_logprob_pt()` and calls it on each of its skip paths at lines 721, 789 and 797.

Scope: this bites when the skipped request itself requested input logprobs (`logprob_start_len >= 0`). With the default `-1` its block is zero rows and the skip is harmless. Overlap scheduling is on by default and retraction is ordinary under KV pressure, so no unusual flag is required.

### Reproduction

Driving the real `process_batch_result_prefill` on CPU with two prefill requests, the first retracted, `extend_input_len_per_req=[2, 3]` and `extend_logprob_start_len_per_req=[0, 0]`, over a flat array of `[-1.0, -2.0, -30.0, -31.0, -32.0]`:

```
expected (active request's own block)  [None, -30.0, -31.0]
actual                                 [None,  -1.0,  -2.0]   <- the retracted request's values
```

I have a regression test that reproduces this, written against the existing `test_batch_result_processor_hidden_states.py` harness and registered as `register_cpu_ci(est_time=2, suite="base-a-test-cpu")`, so it needs no GPU. It fails on `main` and passes with the cursor advanced. I will open a PR with the fix and that test shortly and link it here.

Related but distinct, so neither covers this path:
- [#34153](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34153) applies the same "consume the slice, skip the attach" idea to the `req.to_finish` path, which routes through the normal branch rather than this skip.
- [#36724](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/36724) adds a new `deferred_mm_abort` branch immediately above this `continue` and advances the cursor there, leaving this one unchanged.
- [#32103](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32103) and [#32089](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/32089) describe the hidden-states analog and both cite this logprob path as already correct.

### Environment

`python3 -m sglang.check_env` does not run on a CPU-only host. [`check_env.py:583-594`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/check_env.py#L583-L594) is an `if/elif` chain over `is_cuda_v2()/is_hip()/is_npu()/is_musa()/is_mps()` with no `else`, so `env` is never bound and it exits with `NameError: name 'env' is not defined`. Reporting that separately. Environment collected by hand:

```
sglang commit: 0df69849ba
Python:        3.12.13
OS:            Linux-6.6.87.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2-x86_64-with-glibc2.43
PyTorch:       2.13.0+cpu
transformers:  5.12.1
CUDA available: False
```

The affected code is pure Python request accounting in the scheduler and is exercised by the CPU test suite, so no accelerator is needed to reproduce it.

title: [Roadmap] GLM-5.2 + AMD/ROCm DSpark support
body:
## Goal

Track GLM-5.2 DSpark support on AMD/ROCm and link it to the main DSpark roadmap: #30344.

Primary validation target: AMD MI350, ROCm 7.x, TP4. The implementation should stay generic where possible, but no Hopper/Blackwell claim is made until the same gates run there.

The current RedHat checkpoint is workload-sensitive. This roadmap targets a correct, reusable DSpark runtime contract; it does not claim workload-independent speedup from that checkpoint.

> This issue body is the source of truth. Comments are historical logs and may refer to superseded branches or experiments.

## Current Status

Updated 2026-07-25 UTC.

| Stage | Deliverable | Status |
|---|---|---|
| S0 | Target-only baseline | Green: controlled c16 median `505.73` output tok/s |
| F0 | Functionality, verifier correctness, AR/AL | Green: 256/256 compact gate, seeded sampling, and static verify |
| S1a | Safe draft/target graph admission and eager fallback | Green contract/fallback; the historical S1a c16 arm had `0/436` target replays and is superseded for coverage by S1b/S2 |
| S2 | SPS/confidence scheduling and graph-tier alignment | Green in fork staging; deep TP4 table tuning deferred |
| S3 | STS calibration and table consume | Green scaled fixed-seed gate; not yet a production calibration claim |
| S1b | Regime-neutral target-verify graph plus folded accept/commit | Green on the validated MI350 route in fork staging |
| Runtime | Zero-overhead overlap scheduling | Yellow: pure-TP draft #32374; final controlled A/B pending |
| S4 | GLM-5.2/MI350-specific kernels and hidden/KV fast paths | Not started |

Capability order: `S0 -> F0 -> S1a -> S2/S3 basics -> S1b -> S4`.

The current staging ancestry is implementation-driven: S1b runtime contract (#21) is the base for S2 tier fill (#25) and the S2 logical/physical acceptance contract (#26). Upstream review slices may be split differently.

## PR Review Order

### Upstream

| PR | Scope | State / next action |
|---|---|---|
| #31047 | GLM-5.2 RedHat DSpark config and block contract | Ready for review; merge first |
| #31260 | ROCm functionality/correctness | Draft, validated; rebase and mark ready after #31047 |
| #31457 | Compact/ragged graph contract and guarded fallback | Draft, needs refresh after #31260 |
| #31451 | SPS fit diagnostics | Open; independent tooling review |
| #32186 | DSpark import-side-effect cleanup | Draft, needs rebase/split |
| #32374 | Pure-TP zero-overhead overlap scheduling | Draft; exact-head MI350 A/B pending |

Logical runtime review order:

```text
#31047 config/block contract
  -> #31260 ROCm functionality/correctness
       -> #31457 graph admission/fallback
       -> upstream ports from the validated S1b/S2 staging stack
```

### Validated Fork Staging

- [tanth47/sglang#21](https://github.com/tanth47/sglang/pull/21): S1b target-verify graph contract. One target forward per verify step; whole-batch graph replay or whole-batch eager fallback; folded accept/commit on eligible replays.
- [tanth47/sglang#25](https://github.com/tanth47/sglang/pull/25): S2 exact graph-tier fill using real confidence-ranked verify tokens, with no synthetic token rows.
- [tanth47/sglang#26](https://github.com/tanth47/sglang/pull/26): S2 logical/physical acceptance contract; logical SPS AR/AL is the no-regression gate and filler-inclusive physical AR/AL remains telemetry.

Reference only: #30720 and fork PRs #1-#20 are historical/exploratory. Fork PR #27 is superseded by #32374.

## Current Evidence

### F0 Accuracy

MI350 TP4, fixed seed, natural UltraChat prompts around 2k ISL, `zai-org/GLM-5.2-FP8` plus `RedHatAI/GLM-5.2-speculator.dspark`:

- Compact 256 x 128: 256/256 complete, zero errors, aggregate AR `59.62%`, aggregate AL `5.174`.
- Seeded non-greedy: 16/16 complete at `temperature=0.8`, `top_p=0.95`, exact OSL 128.
- Static verify: 16/16 complete, exact OSL 128.

Accuracy remains a required gate for every cumulative performance PR.

### Controlled Cumulative Ladder

Fixed seed 42, same natural UltraChat fixture, disjoint warmup, c16, 48 measured prompts per repeat, exact OSL 512, `ignore_eos=true`, three repeats.

| Cumulative arm | Median AR | Median AL | Median output tok/s | Target graph |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| S0 target-only | n/a | n/a | 505.73 | n/a |
| S1b / alignment off | 50.70% | 4.534 | 634.78 | 80.9% |
| S2 exact tier fill | 49.75% physical | 4.482 physical | 749.69 | 100% |

S2 is `+18.1%` output throughput versus S1b and `+48.2%` versus S0 in this controlled TP4 scenario. All repeats completed with exact OSL 512 and passed one-target-forward plus folded accept/commit invariants.

The physical AR denominator includes graph-tier filler. PR #26 therefore records both SPS-selected logical lengths and physical execution lengths. Its three-repeat c16 gate completed 144/144 requests with:

- logical AR `50.525%`, logical AL `4.519`;
- physical AR `50.277%`, physical AL `4.519`;
- target graph, folded accept, and folded commit coverage `1332/1332`;
- zero missing sidecars, prefix loss, conservation failures, or bounds violations.

### Profile Direction

On the controlled S2 c16 profile, target verify was `93.4%` of GPU step time. Estimated GPU busy time was about `96.2%`, leaving about `3.8%` bubble. DSpark layout/accept/commit was only `0.3%` of the visible critical path.

Implication: deeper accept/commit folding is not the next measured priority. Finish the controlled zero-overhead A/B, then defer model-compute and communication tuning until the intended serving parallelism is known.

Detailed commands, artifacts, kernel breakdowns, and invariants live in the corresponding PR bodies (#21, #25, #26, and #32374).

## Active Blockers

1. #31047 still requires upstream review.
2. #31260 is validated but remains draft until the config/block-contract dependency is resolved.
3. #31457 and #32186 need refresh against the current upstream stack.
4. #32374 still needs an exact-head MI350 controlled overlap on/off gate.

## Next Actions

1. Get #31047 reviewed and merged.
2. Rebase #31260 onto current `main`, rerun lint plus the focused ROCm gate, then mark it ready for review.
3. Refresh #31457 and port the validated S1b/S2 staging work into small upstream behavior PRs.
4. Finish #32374 with c1 overlap on/off plus a c16 throughput, AR/AL, graph, and folding guard. Keep DP-attention coordination as follow-up.
5. Defer deep SPS table and S4 tuning until the intended serving parallelism is known.

## Evidence Rules

- Fixed seed and natural prompts; do not pad or cut prompts to force ISL.
- Performance gates use exact OSL 512 with `ignore_eos=true`.
- Warm up once per `(dataset, OSL, concurrency)` before measurement.
- Report prompts, errors, AR, AL, output throughput, graph/folded-stage coverage, and target-forward count.
- Each performance PR reports cumulative results. Standalone ablation is optional when a slice cannot run independently.
- Do not claim speedup from startup/JIT-contaminated or otherwise non-comparable runs.

title: [Bug] Large HiCache UCX startup timeout on downstream build; not reproduced on v0.5.20
body:
### Result

**Not reproduced on the latest upstream image (v0.5.20).** A large HiCache pool triggered a UCX startup timeout on our earlier downstream build, but both HiCache and no-HiCache starts passed with the unmodified upstream image.

| Build | HiCache per rank | UCX initialization, all 8 ranks | Server ready |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Downstream `869abc0605`, NIXL 1.3.0 / UCX 1.21.0 | 234 GB | Six ranks explicitly timed out at 60s; none completed | No |
| Same downstream build, no HiCache | 0 | 3–4s | Yes |
| **Upstream v0.5.20, NIXL 1.4.1 / UCX 1.22.0** | **234 GB** | **~2s** | **234s after launch** |
| Same upstream image, no HiCache | 0 | ~2s | 62s after launch |

Each HiCache/control pair ran on the same eight-H200 node with fresh processes. The upstream pair used a different physical node from the downstream pair, and multiple software components changed: this does **not** identify a fix or prove the cause. Only startup was tested, with no inference requests. Both upstream runs registered all eight KV buffers, passed passive `/ready` checks for 30 seconds, and exited cleanly.

### Reproduction settings

8 H200s, approximately 2014 GiB host RAM; public `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite` real weights, revision `604d5664dddd88a0433dbae533b7fe9472482de0`.

Upstream image: `lmsysorg/sglang:latest` resolved to **v0.5.20**, source `94602c9c2b7cbdb8efd5c52802dac6a1c180089e`. Tested amd64 image digest:

```text
lmsysorg/sglang@sha256:b27fce60bc5494c118c4910702812bcfa8cee67abcdd1ff8b0902f21647552f4
```

No source overlay, serving patches, or dependency replacements. Download the model revision above into `$MODEL_DIR`, then run:

```bash
export SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_ENGINE_INIT_TIMEOUT=60
export SGLANG_NCCL_ALL_GATHER_IN_OVERLAP_SCHEDULER_SYNC_BATCH=1
export SGLANG_FORCE_STREAM_INTERVAL=1
export SGLANG_FORCE_CPU_IMAGE_PREPROCESSING=0

python -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path "$MODEL_DIR" --trust-remote-code \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 30000 \
  --tp-size 8 --dp-size 8 --ep-size 8 --enable-dp-attention \
  --disaggregation-mode prefill --disaggregation-transfer-backend nixl \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.7 --dtype bfloat16 --kv-cache-dtype bf16 \
  --page-size 64 --tokenizer-worker-num 4 \
  --context-length 150000 --max-running-requests 1024 \
  --skip-server-warmup --log-level debug --decode-attention-backend fa3 \
  --enable-hierarchical-cache --hicache-size 234 \
  --hicache-write-policy write_through \
  --hicache-mem-layout page_first --hicache-io-backend kernel
```

Remove the five HiCache options for the control. CUDA graphs stay enabled; NIXL is the PD transport, not L3 storage. Actual pool allocation: **234,001,612,800 bytes per rank**, about **1.872 TB total**. Size is per rank and requires sufficient host/cgroup headroom.

### Original failure

The downstream run failed **during UCX backend creation, before KV registration**:

```text
RuntimeError: NIXL create_backend('UCX', {'num_threads': '8'}) did not return within 60s
```

Five seconds before failure: **141.6 GiB host headroom**, **39.2–39.4 GiB free per GPU**, no host OOM-counter increase or CUDA OOM. Host memory pressure and compaction were high. No native stack inside UCX was captured. A later audit found rank 0 in a debugger tracing stop at 21:29:30 UTC, inside the 60-second UCX window, as well as earlier allocation-stage attachments. The retained samples do not establish total pause duration. Other ranks also timed out without a recorded tracing stop, but this run was not free of measurement interference. A telemetry gap further limits the evidence.

The upstream HiCache run kept at least **120 GiB host headroom**, logged no OOM, and completed UCX startup quickly. The underlying reason for the older failure remains unresolved.

<details>
<summary>Upstream runtime</summary>

Python 3.12.3; PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130; NIXL/nixl-cu13 1.4.1; bundled UCX 1.22.0; CUDA 13.0; driver 595.71.05; Linux 6.8.12; FlashInfer 0.6.18; Transformers 5.12.1. THP mode remains `madvise`. The 60-second UCX deadline and eight prefill backend threads were unchanged.

</details>

### Follow-up: the extra host memory is DC receive buffers

On one exclusive node, with the same upstream source/image and **232 GB/rank** HiCache, we compared fresh server processes:

| Native backend | DC interfaces | Receive-buffer chunks | Scheduler anonymous huge pages | UCX startup span |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| NIXL 1.4.1 / UCX 1.22 | 0 | 288 | 12.498 GiB | 2s |
| NIXL 1.3.0 / UCX 1.21 | 288 | 576 | 23.188 GiB | 4s |
| Same 1.3.0 package, only `UCX_TLS=^dc_mlx5` added | 0 | 288 | 12.502 GiB | 3s |

All three initialized all eight ranks, registered KV buffers, and held passive readiness for 30 seconds. No compaction stalls, THP fallbacks, or OOM occurred. No inference or PD transfers were tested. The third case is a diagnostic intervention, **not a verified timeout fix**.

UCX debug logs and per-scheduler memory maps identify the difference: **8 ranks × 9 workers × 4 ports = 288 DC interfaces**, each eagerly allocating a **38 MiB** receive buffer through `rc_recv_desc`. Those extra buffers account for **10.6875 GiB** of huge pages. Excluding only DC on the old package removes them and matches the newer package. Actual loaded UCX versions were verified in server logs.

The old binary includes DC; the new wheel omits it. [NIXL PR 1708](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/nixl/pull/1708) disables DC in the manylinux build. The v1.3.0 source tag also contains that flag despite the tested wheel including DC, so we report observed binary features rather than infer build history from tags.

During the **original failing UCX initialization window**, kernel counters rose by **10,496 compaction attempts, 10,492 failures, 3,407 THP fallbacks, and 3,668 direct-reclaim stalls**. They were flat just before UCX started. The examined SGLang NIXL startup and host-pool files are byte-identical between the downstream and upstream revisions.

This supports a host-memory compaction explanation: after HiCache pins most host RAM, UCX's contiguous huge-page requests become expensive; the old package adds substantial extra demand. **The memory difference is confirmed; the historical timeout's root cause remains unproven.** Both packages pass on this node. A blocked UCX stack or a controlled intervention while the timeout recurs is still missing.

The pool was bounded to 232 GB/rank on this node, below the original 234 GB/rank. Startup spans use one-second logs; the memory-map capture caused one-time sampling gaps of about 13–14 seconds after readiness. Kernel settings, deadline, and serving code were unchanged. No production fix or full PD performance claim is made.


### Original runtime retry without debugger attachment

We also retried the **original fork and original image**, with NIXL 1.3.0 / UCX 1.21.0 and no debugger attachment. With a safely bounded **232 GB/rank** pool, all eight UCX backends completed in **4s**, KV registration succeeded, and passive readiness stayed healthy for 30s. The old build still created 288 DC interfaces and used **23.193 GiB** of scheduler anonymous huge pages. There were **zero compaction stalls, THP fallbacks, or OOMs**, despite minimum total headroom of only **108.54 GiB**.

This shows that the original software can pass with the extra DC buffers intact; the newer image is not a demonstrated timeout fix. Total free RAM alone also does not explain the original failure. This retry used a different physical node and 232 rather than 234 GB/rank, so it does not isolate debugger interference or host fragmentation as the cause. No inference requests were sent; the repro allocation was released after evidence collection.

title: [Bug] Gemma 4 E2B native LoRA adapter load fails with missing lora_A weight
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [ ] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [ ] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [ ] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

Loading a PEFT LoRA adapter trained against `google/gemma-4-E2B-it` into SGLang 0.5.12 via `--lora-paths` fails before `/model_info` readiness with a missing-weight `RuntimeError` for `lora_A` keys on language-tower attention projections.

The adapter was trained with PEFT against explicit Gemma 4 language-tower module names (after an earlier regex `target_modules` attempt was rejected by SGLang's `all` / `all-linear` constraint). The resulting adapter checkpoint contains weights of the form `base_model.model.model.language_model.layers.<N>.self_attn.{q,k,v,o}_proj.lora_{A,B}.weight`, but SGLang's loader fails to locate `lora_A` at the key shape it expects.

This appears to be a PEFT-key to SGLang-internal-name mapping mismatch specific to Gemma 4's `model.language_model.layers.*` nesting.

Merging the adapter into standalone weights outside SGLang and serving the merged model works with Triton attention. The FlashInfer request-time failure is tracked separately in this repo's `docs/issues/flashinfer-bug.md` draft.

### Reproduction

Full repro (commands, fixtures, expected outputs): https://github.com/nemilentsau/sglang-gemma4-triton-fallback — specifically [docs/reproduce-failure.md#3-reproduce-native-lora-failure](https://github.com/nemilentsau/sglang-gemma4-triton-fallback/blob/main/docs/reproduce-failure.md#3-reproduce-native-lora-failure).

Minimal command (after the training step in the linked repo):

```bash
BATCH_SIZE=8 STARTUP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=900 \
  scripts/serving/run-sglang-native-lora-check.sh
```

That script invokes `sglang.launch_server` with `--lora-paths ticket-triage=adapters/google-gemma-4-e2b-it-ticket-triage-lora/905e84b50c4d2a365ebde34e685027578e6728db` against the pinned base model (`google/gemma-4-E2B-it` revision `905e84b50c4d2a365ebde34e685027578e6728db`).

**Expected:** SGLang reaches `/model_info` and the adapter serves.

**Actual:** SGLang exits before readiness with:

```text
RuntimeError: Failed to load LoRA adapter ticket-triage:
'base_model.model.model.language_model.layers.15.self_attn.v_proj.lora_A.weight'
```

Adapter details:
- Trained with PEFT `0.19.1`, rank 8, on a 16-example synthetic ticket-triage fixture (the fixture is intentionally synthetic and is *not* a quality benchmark — it exists only to produce a reproducible Gemma 4 LoRA adapter shape).
- `target_modules` was set to explicit language-tower names after `all-linear` and regex variants did not produce a loadable adapter.

### Environment

Local stack (full details in [docs/observed-results.md](https://github.com/nemilentsau/sglang-gemma4-triton-fallback/blob/main/docs/observed-results.md)):
