- PEFT: `0.19.1`
- FlashInfer: `0.6.11.post1`
- cuDNN: `nvidia-cudnn-cu13==9.19.0.56`
- CUDA driver API: `13000` via `/usr/local/cuda/compat`
- GPU: NVIDIA RTX A6000 (49140 MiB), driver `550.144.03`
- Container: `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.12-cu130-runtime` on Paperspace Gradient

title: [Bug] Gemma 4 31B (attention_k_eq_v) PEFT LoRA adapter fails to load: missing v_proj, wrong per-layer buffer dims, vision-tower tensors collide
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

A PEFT LoRA adapter trained on `google/gemma-4-31B-it` cannot be loaded on current main (f2f223e6). #25913 reported the same family of problem on E2B and was auto-closed as inactive; the 31B case is worse because 31B has layers that E2B does not.

31B facts (from the checkpoint's safetensors headers and config):

| layer type | q_proj rows | k_proj rows | v_proj |
|---|---|---|---|
| sliding_attention (50 layers) | 8192 (32 heads x 256) | 4096 (16 KV heads x 256) | present |
| full_attention (10 layers) | 16384 (32 heads x 512) | 2048 (4 KV heads x 512) | absent (`attention_k_eq_v`) |

A PEFT adapter over the usual seven projections therefore has q and k LoRA weights but no v weight on the 10 full-attention layers, while the other 50 layers have all three.

Three separate failures, in the order you hit them:

1. `--enable-lora` startup: `Gemma4ForConditionalGeneration.get_hidden_dim` reads `head_dim`, `hidden_size`, `intermediate_size` off the top-level `Gemma4Config`, which does not have them.
   ```
   AttributeError: 'Gemma4Config' object has no attribute 'hidden_size'
   ```
   With that patched to read the text config, the buffers still need per-layer head_dim and per-layer KV-head count. Using one KV-head count for all layers gives a 10240-wide qkv buffer on sliding layers whose tensor is 16384 wide (or the reverse, depending on which count you pick).

2. Adapter load: `LoRAAdapter.normalize_qkv_proj` checks once, across the whole adapter, whether `v_proj` exists, then reads it for every layer.
   ```
   KeyError: 'base_model.model.model.language_model.layers.5.self_attn.v_proj.lora_A.weight'
   RuntimeError: Failed to load LoRA adapter ...
   ```
   #28199 keeps the adapter-wide check, so it raises the same error on this adapter.

3. First request with the adapter: PEFT adapters trained on the VLM can also contain vision-tower LoRA tensors (`vision_tower.encoder.layers.N.self_attn.o_proj`, in_features 1152). `LoRAAdapter` buckets tensors by the layer index in the name, so the vision tensor for layer N overwrites the language tensor for layer N in the same bucket.
   ```
   AssertionError: LoRA buffer shape torch.Size([8, 4096]) does not match weight shape torch.Size([8, 1152]).
   ```
   This kills the scheduler.

Fix for all three plus unit tests in #40964, verified on an H100 against HF+PEFT teacher-forced logprobs.

### Reproduction

Train any r=8 PEFT LoRA on `google/gemma-4-31B-it` with `target_modules=["q_proj","k_proj","v_proj","o_proj","gate_proj","up_proj","down_proj"]` (PEFT skips `v_proj` on the k_eq_v layers because the module is `None` there), then:

```bash
python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path google/gemma-4-31B-it --tp 2 \
  --attention-backend triton --enable-lora --max-lora-rank 8 \
  --lora-paths my_adapter=/path/to/adapter
```

Failure 1 happens at startup on main. Failures 2 and 3 appear once 1 is patched (or on the #28199 branch for failure 2). A CPU-only repro of failure 2 with two layers of synthetic weights:

```python
import torch
from sglang.srt.lora.lora import LoRAAdapter
p = "base_model.model.model.language_model.layers.{L}.self_attn.{m}.lora_A.weight"
w = {p.format(L=0, m="q_proj"): torch.ones(2, 3), p.format(L=0, m="k_proj"): torch.ones(2, 3), p.format(L=0, m="v_proj"): torch.ones(2, 3),
     p.format(L=5, m="q_proj"): torch.ones(2, 3), p.format(L=5, m="k_proj"): torch.ones(2, 3)}
LoRAAdapter.normalize_qkv_proj(None, list(w), w)   # KeyError on layer 5 v_proj
```

### Environment

- sglang 0.5.21.dev482+gf2f223e69 (main, editable install), sglang-kernel 0.4.7
- torch 2.13.0+cu130, transformers 5.12.1, peft 0.21.0 (for the reference run)
- Python 3.10.12, Ubuntu 22.04, NVIDIA driver 580.126.20, CUDA 13.0
- 2x H100 80GB (TP=2), bf16, `--attention-backend triton`

title: [Bug] FlashInfer MIS silently overflows uint16 item positions for >65k-token items
body:
### Summary

FlashInfer Multi-Item Scoring (MIS) appears to silently overflow item-position metadata when any scored item is longer than 65,535 tokens.

In `python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/flashinfer_backend.py`, `_process_multi_item_scoring` casts per-item positions to `torch.uint16`, and `max_item_len_ptr` is also built as `uint16`. For a 70k-token scored item, positions wrapped from `65535` back to `0`, the request still returned HTTP 200, and MIS scores diverged materially from the identical non-MIS scoring run.

If FlashInfer requires uint16 metadata here, this looks like a missing validation/fallback bug in SGLang. If FlashInfer supports wider metadata, this looks like a correctness bug in SGLang's MIS metadata construction.

### Environment

- Repo: current `main`, commit `3e255fd49371a810e4fc900b95c7b60f6876ed38`
- Backend: `attention_backend="flashinfer"`
- MIS run: `--enable-mis`
- Comparison run: identical settings without `--enable-mis`
- `--chunked-prefill-size -1`
- `--context-length 80000`
- `--max-total-tokens 90000`
- `--max-prefill-tokens 90000`
- `--disable-cuda-graph`
- `--disable-radix-cache`
- Model used for completed validation: `Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct`
- Hardware used for completed validation: single GCP `NVIDIA A100-SXM4-40GB`

Note: I originally attempted this on a single GCP A100 80GB, but the spot VM was preempted and follow-up A100 80GB capacity/quota was unavailable. The completed run used an A100 40GB fallback, but exercised the same FlashInfer MIS metadata path.

### Repro shape

I used pre-tokenized inputs so item lengths were exact:

- `query_len = 4`
- `item_below_len = 65000`
- `item_long_len = 70000`
- `short_item_len = 16`
- `label_token_ids = [9834, 902]`

Requests tested:

1. non-MIS `score(query, [item_below])`
2. MIS `score(query, [item_below])`
3. non-MIS `score(query, [item_long])`
4. MIS `score(query, [item_long])`
5. MIS `score(query, [short_item_a, item_long, short_item_b])`

### Temporary logging added for validation

I added env-gated debug logging around `_process_multi_item_scoring` to print:

- `delimiter_indices`
- `suffix_len`
- `max(pos_within_item)` before cast
- `token_pos_in_items_ptr` dtype/min/max after cast
- `max_item_len_ptr`
- final scores from MIS and non-MIS paths

### Actual metadata evidence

Below-boundary item did not wrap:

```text
delimiter_indices=[4, 65005] suffix_len=65002 max(pos_within_item)=65000
token_pos_prepad dtype=torch.uint16 min=0 max=65000
token_pos_in_items_ptr dtype=torch.uint16 min=0 max=65000 token_pos_in_items_len=65002 prefix_len_ptr=[4]
max_item_len_ptr dtype=torch.uint16 values=[65000]
```

70k-token item silently wrapped:

```text
delimiter_indices=[4, 70005] suffix_len=70002 max(pos_within_item)=70000
token_pos_prepad dtype=torch.uint16 min=0 max=65535 sample[65532:65542]=[65532, 65533, 65534, 65535, 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5]
token_pos_in_items_ptr dtype=torch.uint16 min=0 max=65535 token_pos_in_items_len=70002 prefix_len_ptr=[4]
max_item_len_ptr dtype=torch.uint16 values=[65535]
```

Mixed-item MIS request also showed truncation for the long item:

```text
delimiter_indices=[4, 21, 70022, 70039] suffix_len=70036 max(pos_within_item)=70000
token_pos_in_items_ptr dtype=torch.uint16 min=0 max=65535 token_pos_in_items_len=70036 prefix_len_ptr=[4]
max_item_len_ptr dtype=torch.uint16 values=[65535]
```

### Score comparison

Below-boundary MIS roughly matched non-MIS:

```text
non-MIS [item_below]: [8.390536297405524e-10, 4.653219071241521e-08]
MIS     [item_below]: [7.075681511711238e-10, 3.9858220603823486e-08]
max_abs_diff: 6.673970108591723e-09
```

Above-boundary MIS materially diverged, while non-MIS returned normally:

```text
non-MIS [item_long]: [1.1668274457666609e-09, 5.28146429567152e-08]
MIS     [item_long]: [4.873932399926735e-10, 2.2988196753904577e-07]
max_abs_diff: 1.7706732458233056e-07
```

The second label score was about `4.35x` larger in MIS than in non-MIS for the 70k-token item.

The mixed MIS request completed in a separate run and returned scores, while logging the same uint16 truncation:

```text
scores=[[1.3688256846912624e-06, 4.630677602424308e-06], [4.580356498790701e-10, 2.0294656015981385e-07], [1.458230590824044e-06, 4.634247233474888e-06]]
```

### Expected behavior

SGLang should not silently produce wrapped MIS metadata for an item longer than 65,535 tokens.

Possible fixes, depending on the FlashInfer contract:

- If FlashInfer requires uint16 item-position metadata, validate item lengths before MIS metadata construction and reject the request or fall back to non-MIS for any item longer than 65,535 tokens.
- If FlashInfer supports wider metadata, construct `token_pos_in_items_ptr` / `max_item_len_ptr` using a sufficiently wide dtype instead of `uint16`.

### Existing issue/PR search

I searched open and closed issues/PRs for:

- `token_pos_in_items_ptr uint16`
- `max_item_len_ptr uint16`
- `Multi-Item Scoring 65535`
- `enable_mis long context`

I did not find an existing bug report. The only relevant hit I found was the merged MIS implementation PR, https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/10979, which documents the MIS metadata fields as uint16 but does not cover this overflow case.

title: [Bug] FP8 KV-cache decode slowdown: unfused K/V quantization + per-layer Q conversion overhead
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [ ] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug


## 1. Problem

When enabling `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3` on Hopper (H200, SM90) with the fa3 backend, **decoding slows down** compared to BF16 KV-cache, especially on small batches and short contexts. The slowdown is caused by **runtime overhead** that is absent on the BF16 path and that is **not eliminated by a static FP8 checkpoint**.

The root cause is architectural: sglang performs FP8 KV-cache quantization as a series of **separate Python-level tensor operations** (multiple kernel launches per layer per step), whereas the BF16 path is a single optimized `store_cache` call. On memory-bound decode with small batches, this overhead outweighs the 2× reduction in KV read traffic.

### Symptom

| Scenario | BF16 KV | FP8 KV (fa3) |
|----------|---------|---------------|
| Small batch (1-8), short context | baseline | **10-30% slower** |
| Small batch, long context (32K+) | baseline | possibly faster |
| Large batch (128+) | baseline | slightly faster |

---

## 2. Bottlenecks & comparison with vLLM

### 2.1. Bottleneck 1: Unfused K/V quantization on cache write

In [`set_kv_buffer`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/bc82b064004f2e17f09db52afeed52cdf53a87be/python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/memory_pool.py#L1784), quantizing K/V to FP8 is **3-4 separate operations**:

```python
# memory_pool.py:1784-1790 — 4 separate kernel launches per layer per step
if cache_k.dtype != self.dtype:
    if k_scale is not None:
        cache_k.div_(k_scale)      # launch 1: in-place divide K
    if v_scale is not None:
        cache_v.div_(v_scale)      # launch 2: in-place divide V
    cache_k = cache_k.to(self.dtype)  # launch 3: cast K → FP8
    cache_v = cache_v.to(self.dtype)  # launch 4: cast V → FP8
```

This is followed by a separate `store_cache` call to write into the paged cache. On the BF16 path, only `store_cache` runs (single optimized kernel).

**vLLM solution:** vLLM fuses quantization **into the cache-write kernel** itself. In [`reshape_and_cache_kernel_flash`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/26ff616bbf43c5c5ecb847589705cebdbff46706/vllm/v1/attention/ops/triton_reshape_and_cache_flash.py#L109), the division by scale and the implicit FP8 cast happen inside the same triton kernel that stores to the paged cache:

```python
# vLLM: 1 kernel launch — load → divide → implicit cast → store
if FP8_KV_CACHE:
    key_tile = key_load if key_load.dtype.is_fp8() else key_load / tl.load(k_scale)
else:
    key_tile = key_load
# ...
tl.store(key_cache_ptr + tgt_idx_k, key_tile, mask=...)  # implicit cast to FP8
```

### 2.2. Bottleneck 2: Per-layer Q→FP8 conversion in fa3 backend

In `forward_decode`, Q is converted to FP8 **on every layer, every step**:

```python
# flashattention_backend.py:1608-1615 — 3 conversions per layer per step
if self.kv_cache_dtype_str != "auto" and layer.head_dim <= 256:
    if layer.k_scale is not None:
        descale_shape = (forward_batch.batch_size, layer.tp_k_head_num)
        k_descale = layer.k_scale.expand(descale_shape)
        v_descale = layer.v_scale.expand(descale_shape)
    q = q.to(self.kv_cache_dtype)              # conversion 1: Q → FP8
    q_rope = q_rope.to(self.kv_cache_dtype)    # conversion 2: q_rope → FP8
    k_rope = k_rope.to(self.kv_cache_dtype)    # conversion 3: k_rope → FP8
```

For a model with ~64 layers, this is **64+ × 3 = ~192 `.to()` launches** per forward pass. Each `.to()` has ~2-5μs launch overhead → **~400-1000μs of pure launch overhead** per decode step, comparable to the entire attention computation on small batches.

**vLLM solution:** vLLM quantizes Q **centrally in the Attention layer** (once), not in each backend. In `Attention.forward`, a single `query_quant` call handles it, and crucially it **fuses with preceding ops via `torch.compile`**:

```python
# vLLM attention.py:511-521 — single quantization, fused via torch.compile
if self.query_quant is not None:
    # quantizing with a simple torch operation enables
    # torch.compile to fuse this into previous ops
    # which reduces overheads during decoding.
    if self.impl.supports_quant_query_input:
        query, _ = self.query_quant(query, self._q_scale)
```

### 2.3. Bottleneck 3: fa3 FP8 decode kernel less optimized than BF16

FA3 split-KV decode with FP8 Q × FP8 KV is a less-tuned path than the primary BF16 path. The `num_splits=0` auto-heuristic `flashattention_backend.py:345` adds a combine-stage overhead.

**vLLM flashinfer on SM90:** completely avoids Q quantization on decode via `resolve_query_dtype` — uses **BF16 Q × FP8 KV** (descale on read), which is both faster and more accurate (single quantization error on KV only).

### 2.4. Tabular comparison: sglang vs vLLM

| Operation | sglang (fa3) | vLLM (flash_attn) | vLLM (flashinfer SM90) |
|-----------|-------------|-------------------|------------------------|
| **Q → FP8 conversion** | ❌ `q.to()` per layer (192+ launches) | ⚠️ `query_quant` once, **fused via torch.compile** | ✅ None (BF16 Q) |
| **q_rope → FP8** | ❌ per layer | ✅ None (handled in kernel) | ✅ None |
| **k_rope → FP8** | ❌ per layer | ✅ None (handled in kernel) | ✅ None |
| **K ÷ scale** | ❌ separate `div_` launch | ✅ **fused in write kernel** | ✅ **fused in write kernel** |
| **V ÷ scale** | ❌ separate `div_` launch | ✅ **fused in write kernel** | ✅ **fused in write kernel** |
| **K → FP8 cast** | ❌ separate `.to()` launch | ✅ implicit cast in `tl.store` | ✅ implicit cast in kernel |
| **V → FP8 cast** | ❌ separate `.to()` launch | ✅ implicit cast in `tl.store` | ✅ implicit cast in kernel |
| **Paged cache write** | separate `store_cache` | **same kernel as quant** | **same kernel as quant** |
| **Kernel launches for K/V write** | **~5** | **1** | **1** |
| **Attention compute** | FP8 Q × FP8 KV | FP8 Q × FP8 KV (descale params) | **BF16 Q × FP8 KV** (descale on read) |
| **Accuracy** | ❌ double quant error (Q+KV) | ❌ double quant error | ✅ single quant error (KV only) |

---

## 3. Proposed changes

### 3.1. Fuse K/V quantization into the cache-write kernel (high impact)

**Goal:** eliminate the 4 separate `div_` + `.to()` launches in `set_kv_buffer`.

**Approach:** extend the existing `store_cache` JIT kernel (or add a triton variant) to accept `k_scale`/`v_scale` and the target dtype, performing the division + cast **inside** the write kernel — exactly as vLLM does in `reshape_and_cache_kernel_flash` .

```python
# Proposed: single fused kernel call instead of div_ + to() + store_cache
store_cache_fp8(
    k, v,
    self.k_buffer[layer_id],
    self.v_buffer[layer_id],
    loc,
    k_scale=k_scale,   # passed into kernel, division fused
    v_scale=v_scale,
    out_dtype=self.dtype,  # FP8 — implicit cast on store
)
```

**Expected benefit:** reduces ~5 kernel launches to 1 per layer per step. On a 64-layer model, this removes ~256 launches per decode step.

**Affected files:**
- `memory_pool.py` — `set_kv_buffer`, `set_kv_buffer_prefix_valid` (line 1877), and the SWA variant (line 2234)
- `sglang/jit.kernel/kvcache` — extend `store_cache` or add `store_cache_fp8`

### 3.2. Centralize Q quantization and enable torch.compile fusion (high impact)

**Goal:** eliminate per-layer `q.to(FP8)` / `q_rope.to(FP8)` / `k_rope.to(FP8)` in `forward_decode` and `forward_extend` in flashattention_backend.py.

**Approach:** move Q quantization out of the backend into the RadixAttention layer (as vLLM does in `Attention.forward` - model_executor/layers/attention/attention.py:511, so it happens **once** and can be **fused with preceding ops** (RoPE, QKV projection) via torch.compile:

```python
# Proposed: in RadixAttention.forward, before calling backend
if self.kv_cache_dtype_str != "auto" and self.supports_quant_query_input:
    # single quantization, fusable with prior ops via torch.compile
    q, _ = scaled_fp8_quant(q, self.q_scale)
    # q_rope / k_rope handled inside the attention kernel, not here
```

Then the fa3 backend receives already-quantized Q and does **no** `.to()` calls.

**Expected benefit:** removes ~192 `.to()` launches per decode step on a 64-layer model; enables compiler fusion.

**Affected files:**
- `flashattention_backend.py` — remove `q.to()` / `q_rope.to()` / `k_rope.to()` from `forward_decode` and `forward_extend`
- RadixAttention layer — add centralized `query_quant`

---

## Summary

The FP8 KV-cache decode slowdown in sglang is caused by **unfused runtime quantization** — separate `div_` + `.to()` launches for K/V and per-layer `q.to(FP8)` conversions. vLLM avoids most of this overhead by (1) fusing K/V quantization into the cache-write kernel and (2) centralizing Q quantization in the Attention layer where it fuses with preceding ops via torch.compile. On SM90, vLLM's flashinfer further avoids Q quantization entirely on decode (BF16 Q × FP8 KV).

The proposed changes would bring sglang's FP8 KV-cache path closer to vLLM's efficiency, with the fused write kernel (3.1) and centralized Q quantization (3.2) providing the largest gains.


### Reproduction

.

### Environment

main

title: [Bug] trtllm_mha for both prefill and decode on H200 (SM90) is accepted in v0.5.20 and returns wrong completions (gpt-oss-120b); v0.5.17 refused it; either half alone is correct
body:
### Summary

On **H200 (SM90)** with the `lmsysorg/sglang` **v0.5.20** image, launching gpt-oss-120b with `--attention-backend trtllm_mha` (i.e. trtllm_mha for **both** prefill and decode) **starts normally, reports `attention_backend='trtllm_mha'` in `/server_info`, serves at normal speed — and returns wrong completions**. The same command on the **v0.5.17** image refuses to start with `ValueError: TRTLLM MHA backend for prefill is only supported on Blackwell GPUs (SM100). Please use a different prefill backend.` So a configuration that used to be rejected became silently incorrect.

Each half alone is correct on v0.5.20: `--prefill-attention-backend trtllm_mha --decode-attention-backend fa3` and `--prefill-attention-backend fa3 --decode-attention-backend trtllm_mha` both pass our correctness probes; only the **both-trtllm_mha** combination fails (whether spelled as the single flag or explicitly).

### Environment

- Image `lmsysorg/sglang@sha256:06e4f2ed21afde4ff513cda65070124e727ba23ccaeff7712b8c40e1097d611f` (= tag `v0.5.20` / `latest` on 2026-09-23); inside: sglang 0.5.20, flashinfer 0.6.18 (python/cubin/jit-cache), torch 2.13.0+cu130, flash-attn-4 4.0.0b19
- Contrast image `lmsysorg/sglang@sha256:16aba8925507e631e1dc1e23d95d026533602591775f6a8db68b74ee99746155` (= tag `v0.5.17`): flashinfer 0.6.15.post1, torch 2.11.0+cu130
- 1 × NVIDIA H200 (143771 MiB), Kubernetes pod, cold caches (`HF_HOME` / `DG_CACHE_DIR` on emptyDir)
- Model: `openai/gpt-oss-120b`, snapshot `b5c939de8f754692c1647ca79fbf85e8c1e70f8a`; no speculative decoding, default KV dtype and memory settings

### Reproduction

```bash
python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path /models/hub/models--openai--gpt-oss-120b/snapshots/b5c939de8f754692c1647ca79fbf85e8c1e70f8a \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30000 --attention-backend trtllm_mha
```
Then, with any OpenAI-compatible client at temperature 0 (`/v1/completions`):

| prompt (paraphrased) | v0.5.20, `--attention-backend trtllm_mha` | default (fa3) |
|---|---|---|
| "What is the capital of France?" | completion stops after **4 tokens, no "Paris"** | correct |
| "List the first five prime numbers." | runs to the 768-token budget, **never produces `2, 3, 5, 7, 11` in order** | correct |
| a short multiplication | correct | correct |

Observed on **5 of 6 fresh boots** of the failing configuration (identical failing prompts each time; on one boot a second pass recovered one of the two). The default server passed all three prompts on **4/4 boots, 8/8 passes**.

### Which half

| flags (v0.5.20) | `/server_info` prefill / decode | our 3-prompt probe |
|---|---|---|
| `--attention-backend trtllm_mha` | trtllm_mha / trtllm_mha | **fails** (4/4 boots) |
| `--prefill-attention-backend trtllm_mha --decode-attention-backend trtllm_mha` | trtllm_mha / trtllm_mha | **fails** |
| `--prefill-attention-backend trtllm_mha --decode-attention-backend fa3` | trtllm_mha / fa3 | passes (2/2) |
| `--prefill-attention-backend fa3 --decode-attention-backend trtllm_mha` | fa3 / trtllm_mha | passes (2/2) |
| default | fa3 / fa3 | passes (8/8) |

### What the server says at startup

Nothing: no warning, no fallback line, no SM90/SM100 message in the boot log of the failing configuration; `server_args` echoes `attention_backend='trtllm_mha'`; CUDA-graph capture logs the same `backend=breakable` (prefill) / `backend=full` (decode) strings as the fa3 server.

### Why report it

A configuration that fails loudly is safe; this one is accepted, fast (a 30-s probe on one boot gave ~+6 % tok/s over fa3 at concurrency 16) and wrong. Any selection process that checks "boots + serves + throughput" will grade it healthy. Either the SM90 guard for the trtllm_mha prefill+decode combination that v0.5.17 had should come back, or the combination needs a fix — and a correctness check for (prefill, decode) backend pairs newly accepted on a GPU generation would catch this class.

### Limitations of this report

One model (gpt-oss-120b: mxfp4 experts, GQA 64/8, head_dim 64, hybrid SWA), one GPU type, one image step in which three components moved together (sglang 0.5.17→0.5.20, flashinfer 0.6.15.post1→0.6.18, torch 2.11→2.13) — we cannot say which change opened the path or broke the numerics. We have not read the v0.5.20 source for the guard; the tables above are observations. n = 6 boots for the failing spelling, 1 boot each for the explicit half-splits.

title: [Bug] Disconnected streaming client leaves a zombie request that decodes to max_tokens and floods "state was deleted in TokenizerManager" (regression from #34160 revert)
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

> Submitted by GLM-5.3

When a streaming client disconnects mid-generation, the scheduler-side request
is never aborted and keeps decoding until `max_tokens`. Every output batch for
that request logs:

```
Received output for rid='...' but the state was deleted in TokenizerManager.
```

at a high rate (observed ~15 lines/s per request, sustained for the entire
remaining generation — in production two zombie requests burned GPU for 15+
minutes and occupied both `--max-running-requests` slots, blocking all new
requests from being scheduled).

Root cause (verified on current `main`):

1. `TokenizerManager.generate_request` has an `except BaseException` cleanup
   that calls `_discard_pending_req_states(obj)`. It was added for failures
   *before* the request reaches the scheduler (e.g. input-length validation),
   but a client disconnect raises `asyncio.CancelledError` — also a
   `BaseException` — so the state of a request that **is running on the
   scheduler** gets popped immediately at disconnect time.

2. The delayed safety net then doesn't fire: `create_abort_task` (attached to
   the `StreamingResponse` as a background task, runs ~2s after teardown)
   calls `abort_request(rid)`, which early-returns on
   `tokenizer_worker_num == 1 and rid not in self.rid_to_state`. The
   `AbortReq` is never dispatched, so the scheduler never learns the client
   is gone and decodes to `max_tokens`; each `BatchStrOutput` for that rid
   hits the deleted-state error path.

This is a regression of 71043b9dbb ("Revert parallel request lifecycle
tracking from #32588", #34160). Before the revert, #32588 handled this
correctly: `_discard_pending_req_states(obj, request_lifecycles)` dispatched
`AbortReq` for every rid whose state had `dispatched == True` **before**
removing the state. The revert deleted the `dispatched` markers and the
abort-then-remove ordering, leaving the orphan window. Presumably not covered
by CI because it requires killing a streaming client mid-generation.

(The `HEALTH_CHECK`-prefixed rid skip next to the error log is a different,
known race — unrelated, see #11925.)

Suggested minimal fix (verified in production, restores the pre-revert
invariant without reintroducing full lifecycle tracking):

1. In `generate_request`, treat cancellation separately and only discard
   state if the request was never dispatched:

```python
        dispatched = False
        try:
            ...
            self._send_one_request(tokenized_obj)
            dispatched = True
            async for response in self._wait_one_response(obj, request):
                yield response
        except (asyncio.CancelledError, GeneratorExit):
            # Client disconnect mid-request: keep the state of a dispatched
            # request so the delayed background abort still finds it; the
            # scheduler's abort echo deletes it cleanly. Discarding here
            # orphans the scheduler-side request, which then decodes to
            # max_tokens.
            if not dispatched:
                self._discard_pending_req_states(obj)
            raise
        except BaseException:
            self._discard_pending_req_states(obj)
            raise
```

2. Add a `force` flag to `abort_request` that bypasses the
   `rid not in self.rid_to_state` early-return, and pass `force=True` from
   `create_abort_task` (the scheduler's `abort_request` handler scans by rid
   prefix and no-ops unknown rids, so force-dispatching is safe — it just
   closes the window where the state was already deleted elsewhere):

```python
    def abort_request(self, rid: str = "", abort_all: bool = False, force: bool = False):
        if not abort_all and not rid:
            ...
            return
        if (
            not abort_all
            and not force
            and get_serving().tokenizer_worker_num == 1
            and rid not in self.rid_to_state
        ):
            return
```

With this patch: disconnect → decode stops within the 2s abort window, zero
error lines; normal streaming completions (`[DONE]`) unaffected.

### Reproduction

Any model; the bug is in the tokenizer-manager layer and is
hardware/model-independent.

1. Launch a server:

```bash
python -m sglang.launch_server --model <any-model> --port 30000
```

2. Start a long streaming generation, then kill the client mid-stream:

```bash
curl -sN http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1/chat/completions \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"<any-model>","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Count from 1 to 5000, one number per line."}],"max_tokens":16000,"stream":true}' &
sleep 10 && kill -9 %1
```

**Actual**: `sglang:num_running_reqs` stays 1 and the request decodes until
`max_tokens`; the log floods with the message above (same rid, repeated many
times per second).

**Expected**: the request is aborted shortly after the disconnect (within the
2s background-abort window) and decode stops.

### Environment

- sglang `main` (regression introduced by 71043b9dbb / #34160, still present
  as of a1f9508dd4; no commit has touched `tokenizer_manager.py` since —
  `except BaseException` cleanup and the guard are at current lines ~825
  and ~1952)
- single GPU, TP=1, `--max-running-requests 2`; speculative decoding enabled
  (DSPARK) on our instance, but nothing here is spec-specific
- reproduced and root-caused on a fork whose `tokenizer_manager.py` is
  unmodified upstream code

title: [RFC] Some details relates to SGLang renderer item 4
body:
Spinning item 4 out of #40920 as suggested.

There are three layers, three different jobs, and the split is implicit:

| Layer | Job for stops | Where |
|---|---|---|
| Engine (Python) | authoritative **detection**: decodes a tail window of output ids per decode step and matches `stop_strs` / `stop_regex_strs`, then locates the exact finish length so the stop is included and speculative overshoot is discarded | `managers/schedule_batch.py` — `tail_str()` `:1725` / `:1734`, `_locate_str_stop_finished_len()` `:1786`, `_check_str_based_finish()` `:1814` |
| Frontend (`rust/sglang-server`) | **cancellation**: `AbortGuard` aborts whatever was not disarmed when the caller drops the connection (mirrors Python's `is_disconnected`) | `api_server/guard.rs`, `api_server/common.rs`, `tokenizer_manager/wiring.rs` |
| Renderer | **stream shaping**: a local `StopStringMatcher` for trimming and `finish_reason`, deliberately not removing stops from the engine request; cancellation is declared a host responsibility | `engine/decode.rs`, `engine/types.rs`, `postprocessing/mod.rs:5` |

1. I tend to keep cancellation in the host, which is also what the renderer's own module docs already say, and keep the *decision* to terminate in the engine. A caller can only stop after it has received and decoded enough text, so caller-side abort is late by construction — exactly the case `_stop_match_tail_len(new_accepted_len)` guards against when speculation accepts several tokens in one step. Caller-side abort should therefore be a safety net, never the only mechanism. The real gap is narrower than "who owns abort": `AbortGuard` covers *disconnect ⇒ abort*, but not *the caller is still reading and wants to finish early*, and there is no public abort route today. That is the primitive worth defining, together with one measurement: when the renderer drops the token stream, does that actually cancel the upstream `/generate` request and trigger `AbortGuard`, and what is the latency from engine-side match to slot release? I would rather measure that than assume it.

2. Engine-side detection is per request inside the batch's decode step, so cost is O(requests × stops) per step with no cross-request interference (`finished_len` is local to the request's own output). Renderer-side matching is per stream and stateful (`pending` buffer for matches spanning chunks), so its cost scales with emitted bytes, not with batch size — the state, not the cost, is what scales. Three things I would write into the contract:

- **per-rid termination must be expressible on the transport.** Today `/generate` is one stream per request, so "close the stream" coincides with "end this request"; once gRPC (item 10) multiplexes rids on a connection it will not. This should be settled before item 10 rather than during it.
- **caps belong in the contract.** `MAX_STOP_COUNT = 32`, `MAX_STOP_REGEX_LEN = 256`, `MAX_STOP_REGEX_COUNT = 32` are already enforced in the renderer's sampling normalization (`preprocessing/sampling.rs`, lines 18, 21 and 24); every entry point that admits a request should agree on them.
- **exactly one trimmer per client path**.

3. I would not add one, for detection. The engine already decodes the tail window with its own tokenizer and has to: only the engine can fix `finished_len` inside a decode step, at the moment speculation accepts extra tokens. A frontend tokenizer would be a second text-interpretation path, and there is same-origin evidence for what that costs — the `/v1/tokenize` comparison in #36718 showed 13 of 468 requests differing between the two tokenizer loaders over Unicode combining marks. On stop matching, that class of divergence means the client sees text that was trimmed differently from what was matched.

Where I do think it *is* a generation concern is trimming and the client-visible `finish_reason` — but it belongs to whichever layer owns the client-visible text, which in the renderer shape is the renderer (it has the tokenizer for rendering anyway, and `GenerationFinishReason` is already its type) and in the direct shape is the Python detokenizer (`trim_matched_stop`, honouring `no_stop_trim`). Since the engine also trims on its own path, the invariant to state is **one trimmer per client path** — otherwise text is eaten twice.

**Coupling with item 7.** If tokenizer instantiation moves to the renderer, the frontend stops holding a tokenizer and "the frontend trims" stops being available at all. Item 4 and item 7 should therefore be sequenced together: decide who holds the tokenizer, then who trims.

**Some questions remain**

- Is a non-disconnect abort actually needed for the served deployments, or is disconnect the only real trigger?
- Should the renderer's matcher be deleted once the engine is authoritative, or does it stay as the trimming owner?
- Does anything rely on the renderer's local detection producing a *different* `finish_reason` than the engine's?

Discussion are welcomed. :)

title: [Bug] Kimi-K3 EP32: severe repetition and accuracy regression with MegaMoE, not observed with DeepEP
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

We observe severe reasoning degeneration when serving Kimi-K3 with MegaMoE on GB300. Switching the Decode backend to DeepEP resolves this behavior in our tests.

Requests initially produce coherent reasoning, then may enter prolonged repetition (hmm, or other words), generate tens of thousands of tokens, and fail to complete the task. This also occurs with approximately 34K input tokens, well below the context limit.

**Observed results**


Decode configuration | DeepSWE score
-- | --
TP8 baseline | 68.14% (77/113)
EP32 + DeepEP | ~65.5%
EP32 + MegaMoE, latest run | 42.48% (48/113)

In the latest MegaMoE run, 57/113 tasks contained long mechanical repetition, versus 0/113 in the TP8 baseline using the same detection rule. All 37 responses exceeding 50K output tokens contained repetitive loops. Some affected tasks eventually passed, so successful completion alone does not indicate normal generation.

### Reproduction

Request settings: temperature=1.0, top_p=0.95, thinking_effort=max.

DeepSWE benchmark case: ofetch-per-origin-circuit-breake__qTK9hR7

Expected: Coherent reasoning and normal task completion, as observed with DeepEP.

Actual: MegaMoE produces excessive reasoning and repetitive loops. We have not identified the underlying cause.

### Environment

**Environment**

- Hardware: NVIDIA GB300, ARM64, CUDA 13.0
- Model: Kimi-K3
- SGLang: internal v0.5.19-based build; also observed with an earlier v0.5.18-based build
- FlashInfer: 0.6.18
- sgl-deep-gemm: 0.1.7, with [DeepGEMM #389](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM/pull/389) and [#441](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM/pull/441) backported
- PD disaggregation using Mooncake
- Prefill: TP8, trtllm_mla
- Decode: 32 GPUs, EP32, Attention TP4 × DP8, CUDA Graph enabled

Relevant Decode arguments:

```
--disaggregation-mode decode \
--tp-size 32 \
--ep-size 32 \
--dp-size 8 \
--enable-dp-attention \
--enable-dp-lm-head \
--moe-a2a-backend megamoe \
--attention-backend cutedsl_mla \
--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \
--mamba-ssm-dtype bfloat16 \
--disable-radix-cache \
--cuda-graph-backend-decode full \
--cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 128 \
--reasoning-parser kimi_k3 \
--tool-call-parser kimi_k3
```

The problem persists with SGLANG_DEEPGEMM_PDL=0. It has also been observed with trtllm_mla and with Triton KDA.

title: [Bug] HiCache + hybrid (SSM/Mamba): failed cudaHostRegister on a secondary host pool aborts the whole instance, and the error path throws TypeError thereby hiding the real rc
body:
### Summary

On sglang `0.5.19` (torch `2.13.0+cu130`, CUDA 13.0, H20), starting a **hybrid SSM/Mamba** model
with `--enable-hierarchical-cache --hicache-storage-backend dynamic` fails during
`attach_hybrid_pool_to_unified_cache` and **kills the entire instance**.

Two coupled defects:

1. **`cudaHostRegister` failure is treated as fatal.** `alloc_with_host_register` raises, which
   aborts scheduler init for all TP ranks. But the failure only means "this host pool is not
   zero-copy registered" — and sglang's own non-zero-copy path (`_generic_page_get/_set`) is
   fully functional without registration. A missing acceleration is escalated into a full outage.
2. **The error path destroys its own diagnostic.** Inside the `raise`, `cudart.cudaGetErrorString(rc)`
   is called with a **plain `int`**, which raises `TypeError` on this torch build — so the real
   `rc`/`offset`/`size` are swallowed. Operators only see a bare `TypeError`.

Additionally, the failure **leaves a sticky CUDA error**, which then surfaces later at an unrelated
call site (`_create_sync_groups` → `all_gather_object` → `torch.zeros`), which made this
considerably harder to root-cause.

### Environment

- sglang `0.5.19`
- torch `2.13.0+cu130`, CUDA 13.0
- 8 × H20 (96 GiB) / 8 × H20-3e (141 GiB), driver `535.161.08`
- Model: `Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8` (`Qwen3_5MoeForConditionalGeneration`, pool stack **KV + MAMBA**)
- Backend: `--hicache-storage-backend dynamic` with `interface_v1: 1` in the extra config
  (this selects the zero-copy page functions; the crash itself is in host-pool allocation and is
  not specific to any particular dynamic backend)
- Relevant flags: `--mamba-full-memory-ratio 0.37 --mamba-radix-cache-strategy extra_buffer_lazy
  --mamba-ssm-dtype bfloat16 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --hicache-mem-layout page_first_direct
  --hicache-io-backend direct --tp 8`

### Reproduction

```bash
python -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path <hybrid SSM/Mamba model, e.g. Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8> \
  --tp-size 8 --trust-remote-code \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.80 \
  --enable-hierarchical-cache --hicache-ratio 1.0 \
  --hicache-storage-backend dynamic \
  --hicache-mem-layout page_first_direct \
  --hicache-io-backend direct \
  --mamba-full-memory-ratio 0.37 \
  --mamba-radix-cache-strategy extra_buffer_lazy \
  --mamba-ssm-dtype bfloat16 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \
  --hicache-storage-backend-extra-config '{"backend_name":"...","module_path":"...","class_name":"...","interface_v1":1,...}'
```

Failures are **not deterministic per machine** — we observed the same config **succeed on a 96 GiB
box and fail on a 141 GiB box**, consistent with a pool-geometry / allocation-order dependence.

### Observed failure trace (verbatim)

```
[TP5] attach_hybrid_pool_to_unified_cache failed
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File ".../mem_cache/hybrid_cache/hybrid_pool_assembler.py", line 1759, in attach_hybrid_pool_to_unified_cache
    result = strategy.build(
  File ".../hybrid_pool_assembler.py", line 1329, in build
    host_pool_group, cache_controller = build_hybrid_mamba_stack(
  File ".../hybrid_pool_assembler.py", line 735, in build_hybrid_mamba_stack
    kv_host_pool = build_kv_host_pool(
  File ".../hybrid_pool_assembler.py", line 160, in build_kv_host_pool
    return kv_host_pool_cls(
  File ".../mem_cache/pool_host/mha.py", line 89, in __init__
    super().__init__(
  File ".../mem_cache/pool_host/base.py", line 205, in __init__
    self.kv_buffer = self.init_kv_buffer()
  File ".../mem_cache/pool_host/mha.py", line 191, in init_kv_buffer
    buffer = alloc_func(
  File ".../mem_cache/pool_host/common.py", line 235, in alloc_with_host_register
    _cuda_host_register(buffer, registration_granularity_bytes)
  File ".../mem_cache/pool_host/common.py", line 163, in _cuda_host_register
    f"{cudart.cudaGetErrorString(rc)}) at offset={offset} size={size} "
       ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
TypeError: cudaGetErrorString(): incompatible function arguments. The following argument types are supported:
    1. (arg0: torch._C._cudart.cudaError) -> str
Invoked with: 1                      <-- the real rc is only visible here, by accident
```

A second, later-surfacing variant of the same root cause (sticky CUDA error), reached when the
first pool *does* register successfully:

```
[TP6] Scheduler hit an exception: ...
  File ".../mem_cache/hybrid_cache/hybrid_cache_controller.py", line 161, in attach_storage_backend
    super().attach_storage_backend(
  File ".../managers/cache_controller.py", line 590, in attach_storage_backend
    self.prefetch_hits_sync_groups = self._create_sync_groups()
  File ".../managers/cache_controller.py", line 415, in _create_sync_groups
    create_custom_parallel_group(
  File ".../distributed/parallel_state.py", line 2762, in create_custom_parallel_group
    torch.distributed.all_gather_object(gathered_configs, local_config)
  File ".../torch/distributed/distributed_c10d.py", line 3506, in all_gather_object
    object_sizes_tensor = torch.zeros(
torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: invalid argument
```

Note `cache_controller.py:590` calls `_create_sync_groups()` **immediately** after the storage
backend is attached — i.e. right where the sticky error from a failed registration lands.

### Minimal evidence that this is the registration call

Instrumenting `_cuda_host_register` on the failing box (141 GiB) shows the KV pool registers fine
and a **secondary** pool is the one that fails:

```
reg#1 total=49676820480 (46.27GiB) granularity=3840        -> OK
reg#2 total=17765498880 (16.55GiB) granularity=11796480    -> FAILED rc=1 (cudaErrorInvalidValue) at offset=0
reg#3 total=623738880  ( 0.58GiB) granularity=414720       -> (never reached)
```

`offset=0`, the size is page aligned, and `chunk_limit=256 GiB` (i.e. a single call) — so this is
**not** an alignment, chunking, or size problem. The same three pools register fine in an
otherwise-idle process, so it is state/order dependent within the real init sequence.

### Minimal standalone reproduction of the underlying CUDA behaviour

The failure mode we traced back to is: calling `cudaHostRegister` on memory that is **already
pinned** returns `cudaErrorInvalidValue(1)` (not `cudaErrorHostMemoryAlreadyRegistered(712)`),
and leaves a sticky error that breaks the next unrelated CUDA call:

```python
import torch
cudart = torch.cuda.cudart()
print("baseline:", float((torch.ones(1024, device="cuda") * 2).sum()))   # works

SZ = 256 * 1024 * 1024
t = torch.empty(SZ, dtype=torch.uint8, pin_memory=True)                   # already pinned
rc = int(cudart.cudaHostRegister(t.data_ptr(), SZ, 0))
print("rc =", rc)                                                          # -> 1 (cudaErrorInvalidValue)

# now any CUDA op fails once:
torch.ones(1024, device="cuda") * 2     # -> AcceleratorError: CUDA error: invalid argument
```
Output on our box:
```
baseline: 2048.0
rc = 1
... torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: invalid argument
```

### Why we believe the `raise` is not the intended trade-off

`attach_storage_backend` explicitly keeps a **non-zero-copy** default and only opts into
zero-copy afterwards:

```python
self.page_get_func = self._generic_page_get        # default, works without registration
self.page_set_func = self._generic_page_set
if self.storage_backend_type in [...] or (
        self.storage_backend_type == "dynamic"
        and bool(self.storage_config.extra_config.get("interface_v1", 0))):
    self.page_get_func = self._page_get_zero_copy
    self.page_set_func = self._page_set_zero_copy
```

`_generic_page_get` stages through a dummy page and copies in
(`set_from_flat_data_page(...)`) — it does **not** require the host pool to be
`cudaHostRegister`-ed. So "registered" and "correct" are decoupled here: losing the registration
costs the zero-copy fast path, not correctness. Raising therefore converts a **performance
degradation** into an **instance-wide outage**.

The warning text in the raise ("*host buffer is not pinned and device transfers may silently
return stale data*") suggests the intent is to **prevent silent stale reads** — but (a) the
diagnostic it tries to emit is destroyed by the `cudaGetErrorString(int)` `TypeError`, and
(b) there is no degraded path, even though one exists and is safe.

### Suggested fix

**1. Do not `raise` on registration failure — degrade to the non-zero-copy path (main fix).**

```python
rc = int(cudart.cudaHostRegister(ptr, size, 0))
if rc != 0:
    logger.warning(
        "cudaHostRegister failed (rc=%d) at offset=%d size=%d; "
        "this host pool will not be used for zero-copy transfers",
        rc, offset, size,
    )
    _clear_sticky_cuda_error()   # see (2)
    return                        # fall back to the non-registered path
```

**2. Consume the sticky CUDA error before returning**, otherwise the very next collective
(`_create_sync_groups` → `all_gather_object` → `torch.zeros`) still fails. On this torch build a
subsequent CUDA call is enough to consume it, e.g.

```python
try:
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
except Exception:
    pass
```

**3. Fix the error path itself** — pass a `cudaError`, not a raw `int`
(and never let the diagnostic throw):

```python
from torch._C import _cudart
...
f"cudaHostRegister failed (rc={rc}, "
f"{cudart.cudaGetErrorString(_cudart.cudaError(rc))}) at offset={offset} ..."
```

**4. Consider an explicit escape hatch to disable host registration for CUDA.**
`ALLOC_MEMORY_FUNCS` only maps `npu`/`musa` to `alloc_with_pin_memory`;
on CUDA there is currently no way to opt out other than `SGLANG_HICACHE_HOST_REGISTER_CHUNK_GB`
(which only changes chunking — we verified setting it to `1` does **not** avoid this failure).

### Evidence that each proposed fix is sound (verified on the failing box)

**Claim 1 — host memory works without `cudaHostRegister` (so degrading is safe).**
Tested each in a fresh process (to avoid sticky-error cross-contamination):

```
mode=pin   (torch pin_memory, no cudaHostRegister at all)
  sum = 4096.0  (expect 4096.0)   is_pinned = True    RESULT: OK

mode=mmap  (plain unregistered host memory, is_pinned = False)
  sum = 4096.0                    RESULT: OK
```
⇒ Neither pinned nor unregistered host memory needs `cudaHostRegister` to move data to the GPU.
Losing the registration only removes the zero-copy fast path.

**Claim 2 — `cudaGetErrorString` needs a `cudaError`, not an `int`.**
```
cudaGetErrorString(1)                    -> TypeError: incompatible function arguments
cudaGetErrorString(_cudart.cudaError(1)) -> "invalid argument"        # correct
```

**Claim 3 — a failed registration leaves a sticky error; `synchronize()` clears it.**
```
baseline GPU op                                  -> 1024.0
cudaHostRegister(already-pinned, 64MiB)         -> rc=1
next GPU op                                     -> AcceleratorError: CUDA error: invalid argument
torch.cuda.synchronize()                        -> ok
GPU op after synchronize()                      -> 1024.0            # recovered
```

**Claim 4 — `cudaHostUnregister` also returns rc=1 while sticky** (so cleanup of a failed
registration cannot be relied upon to recover the state):
```
cudaHostUnregister(same buffer) -> cudaErrorInvalidValue(1)
```

### Why the existing unit tests did not catch this

`test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_hicache_host_register.py` (added together with the chunked
registration work) covers the chunking / alignment / rollback logic thoroughly, but two gaps
explain why the real-world failure still slips through:

1. **The failure path is asserted as intended behaviour.** `test_registration_failure_rolls_back_prior_chunks`
   uses `assertRaisesRegex(RuntimeError, "offset=1073741824")` — i.e. the test *encodes* that a
   failed registration must raise. So the question "should it degrade instead of raising?" is a
   **design decision already locked in by a test**, not an oversight I am reporting as a bug.
   (Either way, I'd argue it is the wrong trade-off for the reasons in the Summary — but it is a
   design discussion, so I'm flagging it as such.)
2. **The fake `cudart` accepts an `int` for `cudaGetErrorString`, hiding the real signature:**
   ```python
   class _FakeCudart:
       def cudaGetErrorString(self, rc: int) -> str:      # permissive: accepts int
           return "injected error"
   ```
   The real object is
   `torch._C._cudart.cudart.cudaGetErrorString(arg0: torch._C._cudart.cudaError) -> str`
   and raises `TypeError` when given an `int`. Because the mock is permissive, the `TypeError`
   inside the `raise` can never surface in CI — yet that is precisely the error users see in the
   field, and it is what hides `rc`/`offset`/`size`.

### Affected code ownership (from `git log`, in case it helps routing)

- `_cuda_host_register` / `alloc_with_host_register` + `SGLANG_HICACHE_HOST_REGISTER_CHUNK_GB`
  came in with **#36798 "[HiCache] Align chunked CUDA host registrations"** (@HZY-Wade), which also
  added the unit test discussed above. That PR's own motivation mentions the same
  `invalid argument` failure mode we are hitting.
- The hybrid pool assembly path (`attach_hybrid_pool_to_unified_cache` /
  `build_hybrid_mamba_stack`) and `pool_host/base.py` are from the unified-memory HiCache work
  (@ch-wan).
- The failing line `attach_storage_backend` → `_create_sync_groups()` in
  `managers/cache_controller.py` is in the HiCache controller (@alphabetc1, @ch-wan).

Pinging @HZY-Wade and @ch-wan as the most likely owners of the affected code — apologies if this
is not your area, and feel free to redirect.

### Impact

- **Hybrid SSM/Mamba models** (which instantiate **multiple** host pools — KV + Mamba/SWA + conv)
  are much more exposed than single-pool attention models, because each additional pool is
  another chance to hit the failing registration. This makes HiCache L3 unusable for that model
  family on affected hardware, with a hard crash rather than a performance warning.
- For production this is a availability issue, and it is **not** diagnosable from the surfaced
  error alone.

### Notes / limitations of this report

- The design-intent reading above is inferred from docstrings, comments, the error text, and the
  existence of the non-zero-copy path — it is not confirmed by maintainers.
- We observed the behaviour on sglang `0.5.19` + torch `2.13.0+cu130`; we have **not** checked
  whether a newer sglang/torch already addresses it.
- We have **not** yet validated end-to-end that "degrade instead of raise" + "clear sticky error"
  yields a fully serving instance on the affected box. What *is* individually verified is:
  the registration failure and its `rc`, the destroyed diagnostic, the sticky error and its
  clearing, and that host memory does not need registration to be usable.
- The exact reason the *second* pool's registration fails is still not fully isolated. It is
  **not** page alignment (`offset=0`), **not** a single-call size limit (64 GiB registers fine
  standalone), **not** a cumulative-size cap (46 GiB then 16 GiB succeeds in a fresh process),
  and **not** chunking (`SGLANG_HICACHE_HOST_REGISTER_CHUNK_GB=1` does not avoid it). It appears
  to depend on process state / allocation order during real init.

title: ValueError: pool memory leak detected! crash with LMCache (MP mode) + EAGLE speculative decoding after a load-back hit (page_size > 1)
body:
## Environment

- SGLang v0.5.20 (ROCm, 8x MI300-class GPUs); the code path is platform-independent
- Model: Kimi-K2.6 (MLA), `--tp 4`, `--speculative-algorithm EAGLE3` with the official EAGLE3 draft (`kimi-k2.6-eagle3-mla`)
- `--enable-lmcache` with LMCache running in MP mode (external LMCache daemon), `--page-size 16`
- The bug is model-independent: any EAGLE-family model + LMCache MP mode + `page_size > 1` triggers it

## Symptom

After a request hits the LMCache external KV store (RETRIEVE / load-back into GPU memory), the scheduler crashes at the next idle invariant check on **all TP ranks simultaneously**:

```
ValueError: pool memory leak detected! [full] total=95904, available=95520, evictable=640, protected=0, session_held=0, uncached=0
```

`available + evictable = 96160 > total = 95904`: 256 tokens (16 pages x 16 tokens/page) are double-counted in `evictable_size_`.

## Root cause

`LMCRadixCache.match_prefix` (`sglang/srt/mem_cache/storage/lmcache/lmc_radix_cache.py`) builds the MP load-back marker key from a local `key` variable that is **not bigram-normalized**:

```python
key = params.key
if self.page_size != 1:
    aligned_len = len(key) // self.page_size * self.page_size
    key = key[:aligned_len]            # slice copy made BEFORE normalization
base_res = super().match_prefix(params)  # base class flips params.key.is_bigram IN PLACE
...
self._mp_load_back_markers[req.rid] = _LMCacheLoadBackMarker(
    key=RadixKey(token_ids, key.extra_key, key.is_bigram, ...)
)
```

- The insert path (`RadixCache.cache_finished_req` -> `insert`) normalizes the key: `maybe_to_bigram_view(self.is_eagle)` then `page_aligned`. With EAGLE on, every node in the radix tree is stored with `is_bigram=True`.
- The base `RadixCache.match_prefix` normalizes `params.key` **in place** (`key.maybe_to_bigram_view(self.is_eagle)`), but the local slice in `LMCRadixCache.match_prefix` was copied **before** that flip.
- With `page_size == 1` the local `key` is just an alias of `params.key`, so it accidentally follows the in-place flip and the bug does not trigger. With `page_size > 1` the slice copy stays `is_bigram=False` forever.
- The marker key flows into `_finish_load_back`, where `key[start:end].child_key(self.page_size)` produces raw-token tuples instead of bigram pairs. These never compare equal to the bigram child keys already inserted by `cache_finished_req`, so the load-back attaches a **second radix node covering the same token range**, and `evictable_size_ += fetched` double-counts those tokens.
- At the next idle pass, `SchedulerInvariantChecker._check_all_pools` sees `available + evictable > total` and raises.

## Trigger conditions (all required)

1. EAGLE / EAGLE3 speculative decoding (`is_eagle=True`)
2. LMCache enabled in MP mode (external daemon; the load-back path is active)
3. A load-back hit: a request whose prefix already exists in the LMCache store (warm cache / re-running the same prompt)
4. `page_size > 1` (with `page_size == 1` the non-normalized copy happens to alias the normalized key, masking the bug)

## Reproduction

1. Start the engine: Kimi-K2.6, `--tp 4`, EAGLE3 draft, `--enable-lmcache` (MP mode), `--page-size 16`
2. Run one request that stores its KV, e.g.
   `sglang.bench_serving --dataset-name random --random-input 8192 --random-output 256 --num-prompt 1` (default `--seed 42`)
3. Run the same request again (same seed -> same prompt -> load-back hit). The engine crashes at the next idle check. If the server warmup request itself hits previously stored KV, the crash happens during startup — no bench needed.

Fixed by #40733.

title: [Bug] Triton kernel load_binary fails with "operation not permitted" during decode CUDA graph replay (QSA graph_metadata) on GB10/SM121, cascades into GPU-memory exhaustion and a full driver lockup requiring hard reboot
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

## Summary

On a single DGX Spark (GB10, SM121), running `Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4` under `sglang serve`, the scheduler crashed with `RuntimeError: Triton Error [CUDA]: operation not permitted` inside `_qsa_graph_layout_kernel` during decode CUDA-graph replay, after roughly 24 hours of stable serving. The crash itself was handled (SIGQUIT, attempted clean shutdown), but the GPU memory from the dead process was not released. Docker's `--restart unless-stopped` policy relaunched the container within about a minute, before the driver had recovered, and the new process's allocation attempts failed repeatedly with `NV_ERR_NO_MEMORY`. Shortly after, the NVIDIA driver's internal RM API lock became stuck, held by an `sglang::schedul` thread, which blocked every other process sharing the GPU — including the desktop's own `nvidia-modeset` driver. The entire machine (not just the container) became unresponsive and required a hard power-cycle to recover; it was frozen for approximately 9.5 hours before being manually reset.

## Hardware / Environment

- **Hardware:** DGX Spark (GB10, SM121, unified memory)
- **Driver:** NVIDIA 580.159.03, CUDA 13.0
- **Kernel:** Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS, `6.17.0-1021-nvidia`
- **Docker image:** `lmsysorg/sglang:dev-cu13-qwen38flashnext`
- **Build commit:** `593134d17a6eb0d0fc5f71a970cd2e9dc8e26e8b`
- **Model:** `nvidia/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4`, `--quantization modelopt_fp4`
- **Launch config (relevant excerpt):** `tp_size=2`, `attention_backend=flashinfer`, `linear_attn_backend=triton`, `mamba_backend=triton`, decode CUDA graph enabled (`cuda_graph_config.decode.backend=full`), prefill CUDA graph auto-disabled (multimodal incompatibility)
- No `Xid` driver fault codes were logged around the incident — this does not appear to be an ECC/hardware fault.

## Steps to Reproduce

Not reliably reproducible on demand; occurred once after ~24 hours of otherwise-normal serving (periodic health checks + light request traffic). Suspect it is related to sustained CUDA-graph replay of the QSA (Qwen Sparse Attention) decode path on SM121 — see related issues below, which document other GB10/SM121-specific instability in the same subsystem.

## Actual Behavior — Full Timeline (times below are UTC as logged by the container; local timezone PDT = UTC-7)

**1. Initial fault** — `2026-09-23 06:32:47 TP0`:
```

    attn_backend.init_forward_metadata_out_graph(fb_view)
  File ".../sglang/srt/layers/attention/hybrid_linear_attn_backend.py", line 1047, in init_forward_metadata_out_graph
    attn_backend.init_forward_metadata_out_graph(
  File ".../sglang/srt/layers/attention/qwen_sparse_attn_backend.py", line 751, in init_forward_metadata_out_graph
    self._replay_cuda_graph_metadata(
  File ".../sglang/srt/layers/attention/qwen_sparse_attn_backend.py", line 941, in _replay_cuda_graph_metadata
    self._replay_cuda_graph_metadata_gpu(
  File ".../sglang/srt/layers/attention/qwen_sparse_attn_backend.py", line 1056, in _replay_cuda_graph_metadata_gpu
    launch_graph_metadata(
  File ".../sglang/srt/layers/attention/qsa/graph_metadata.py", line 185, in launch_graph_metadata
    _qsa_graph_layout_kernel[(bs + 1,)](
  File ".../triton/runtime/jit.py", line 370, in <lambda>
    return lambda *args, **kwargs: self.run(grid=grid, warmup=False, *args, **kwargs)
  File ".../triton/runtime/jit.py", line 760, in run
    launch_metadata = kernel.launch_metadata(grid, stream, *bound_args.values())
  File ".../triton/compiler/compiler.py", line 485, in launch_metadata
    self._init_handles()
  File ".../triton/compiler/compiler.py", line 468, in _init_handles
    self.module, self.function, self.n_regs, self.n_spills, self.n_max_threads = driver.active.utils.load_binary(
RuntimeError: Triton Error [CUDA]: operation not permitted

[06:32:47] SIGQUIT received. signum=None, frame=None. It usually means one child failed.
[06:32:47] Sleeping 5 seconds before crash diagnostics to let GPU activity settle.
[06:32:52] No live scheduler processes found; skipping py-spy and CUDA coredump.
[06:32:52] kill_process_tree called: parent_pid=1, include_parent=True, pid=1
```

**2. Automatic restart into a still-broken GPU state** — `2026-09-23 06:38:06` to `06:39:07` (~5 minutes later, after Docker's `unless-stopped` policy relaunched the container):
```
NVRM: nvCheckOkFailedNoLog: Check failed: Out of memory [NV_ERR_NO_MEMORY] (0x00000051)
  returned from _memdescAllocInternal(pMemDesc) @ mem_desc.c:1359
```
(repeated dozens of times over ~1 minute, plus one instance from `rmStatus @ system_mem.c:356`)

**3. Driver-level deadlock** — `2026-09-23 06:43:38`:
```
INFO: task nvidia-modeset/:2496 blocked for more than 122 seconds.
      Tainted: G           O        6.17.0-1021-nvidia #21-Ubuntu
task:nvidia-modeset/ state:D stack:0 pid:2496 tgid:2496 ppid:2
 os_acquire_rwlock_read+0x50/0xe8 [nvidia]
 portSyncRwLockAcquireRead+0x10/0x30 [nvidia]
 rmapiLockAcquire+0x26c/0x2f0 [nvidia]
 ...
INFO: task nvidia-modeset/:2496 <reader> blocked on an rw-semaphore likely owned by task sglang::schedul:546372 <writer>
      os_acquire_rwlock_write+0x50/0xe8 [nvidia]
      portSyncRwLockAcquireWrite+0x10/0x30 [nvidia]
      rmapiLockAcquire+0x1f8/0x2f0 [nvidia]
      ...
```

**4. Full freeze.** Kernel log goes essentially silent immediately after step 3. The machine did not recover on its own; the next boot record is ~9.5 hours later, consistent with a required hard power-cycle. No `Xid` codes were logged at any point.

## Expected Behavior

At minimum, a fatal error in one inference request should not be able to deadlock the NVIDIA driver for the entire machine (including unrelated processes like the desktop compositor). Additionally, the automatic container restart should not begin reallocating GPU memory before confirming the driver has actually released the prior process's allocations, since that retry-into-a-bad-state appears to be what triggered the subsequent lock contention.

## Possibly Related Issues

- #36558 — QSA decode has no working kernel path on SM121 (GB10 / DGX Spark); different failure mode (resolver gate rejects SM121 entirely) but same subsystem (QSA) and same hardware.
- #37633 — CUDA illegal memory access in QSA extend forward at high concurrency, suppressed by `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` / `--disable-overlap-schedule`.
- #19799 — Triton attention + CUDA graphs crash on GB10/sm_121a with illegal memory access on warmup; closed with `--disable-cuda-graph` as the confirmed workaround. Same hardware and failure category (Triton kernel + CUDA graph replay crash on SM121), though a different specific error and crash point than this report.
- PR #38851 — Fixes memory-safety bugs (uninitialized scratch buffer, int32 offset overflow) in the QSA paged sparse-decode gather kernel (`sparse_attn.py`, `qwen_sparse_attn_backend.py`). Does not appear to touch `graph_metadata.py`/`_qsa_graph_layout_kernel`, so likely does not cover this specific crash site, but establishes that this subsystem has known, actively-being-fixed memory-safety issues on this hardware.
- #11658 — DGX Spark (GB10, sm_121a) support tracking issue; confirms GB10 support is still incomplete/in development as of this report.

## Workaround Applied

- Disabled decode CUDA graph capture (`--disable-decode-cuda-graph`) as a stability mitigation, based on the precedent in #19799, trading some decode throughput for avoiding this crash class.
- Configured `kernel.hung_task_panic=1` / `kernel.panic=10` at the OS level so that if the driver deadlocks again, the machine auto-reboots within roughly two minutes instead of hanging indefinitely until a manual power-cycle.

Neither of these addresses the root cause in Triton/sglang; they only bound the blast radius. Filing this primarily so the `load_binary`/`operation not permitted` failure mode in `graph_metadata.py` is tracked, and so the driver-lockup-on-OOM-retry pattern (step 2→3 above) is visible to maintainers who may want to gate the container restart on confirmed GPU recovery, independent of the original Triton fault.

### Reproduction

## Steps to Reproduce

Not reliably reproducible on demand; occurred once after ~24 hours of otherwise-normal serving (periodic health checks + light request traffic). Suspect it is related to sustained CUDA-graph replay of the QSA (Qwen Sparse Attention) decode path on SM121 — see related issues below, which document other GB10/SM121-specific instability in the same subsystem.

title: [Bug] Inkling multimodal returns HTTP 500 instead of 400 for invalid image input
body:
## Summary

When an Inkling model receives invalid multimodal input via `/v1/chat/completions` - an empty/unreachable `image_url`, or an image in an unsupported/corrupted format - the server responds with HTTP 500 instead of HTTP 400. This makes it impossible for a client to distinguish its own bad request from a genuine server fault, and pollutes server-error monitoring with what are really client input errors.

Root cause: `InklingMultimodalProcessor` overrides `process_mm_data_async()` with its own media-resolution step (`_resolve_media_item()`, in `sglang/srt/multimodal/processors/inkling.py`) and its own image-decode step (`_encode_image_bytes()`, in `sglang/srt/multimodal/inkling/image_processing.py`). Neither goes through `BaseMultimodalProcessor._load_single_item()` / `sglang/srt/utils/common.py::load_image()`, so the `CLIENT_MEDIA_EXCEPTIONS` classification added there by #31417 (which every other VLM processor inherits) never applies to Inkling.

## Reproduction

Two ways to reproduce, below.

### Option 1: Exercised directly

No server or model weights needed -- both functions can be exercised directly.

```python
from sglang.srt.multimodal.processors.inkling import _resolve_media_item
from sglang.srt.multimodal.inkling.image_processing import _encode_image_bytes

# 1. Empty image_url -- should be a client error, raises an unclassified one
_resolve_media_item({"url": ""})

# 2. Unreachable image_url -- requests.exceptions.ConnectionError propagates raw
_resolve_media_item({"url": "https://unreachable.example/x.png"})

# 3. Undecodable image bytes -- PIL.UnidentifiedImageError propagates raw
_encode_image_bytes(
    b"definitely not an image",
    patch_size=14,
    rescale_image_frac=None,
    rescale_image_max_upscaled_long_edge=None,
)
```

Each call raises without being reclassified to `ValueError`.

### Option 2: Deploy Inkling and call the API

```bash
sglang serve \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --model-path thinkingmachines/Inkling-NVFP4 \
  --tp 8 \
  --quantization modelopt_fp4 \
  --attention-backend fa4 \
  --page-size 128 \
  --fp4-gemm-backend flashinfer_trtllm \
  --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_trtllm_routed \
  --enable-torch-symm-mem \
  --mamba-radix-cache-strategy extra_buffer \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.85 \
  --swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.1 \
  --mamba-full-memory-ratio 0.1 \
  --enable-multimodal \
  --reasoning-parser inkling \
  --tool-call-parser inkling \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 30000

# 1. Empty image_url
curl -s http://localhost:30000/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "thinkingmachines/Inkling-NVFP4",
    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": [
      {"type": "text", "text": "describe this image"},
      {"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": ""}}
    ]}]
  }'
# Expected: 400. Actual: 500.

# 2. Unreachable image_url
curl -s http://localhost:30000/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "thinkingmachines/Inkling-NVFP4",
    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": [
      {"type": "text", "text": "describe this image"},
      {"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": "https://unreachable.example/x.png"}}
    ]}]
  }'
# Expected: 400. Actual: 500.

# 3. Unsupported/corrupted image format (base64 of non-image bytes)
curl -s http://localhost:30000/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "thinkingmachines/Inkling-NVFP4",
    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": [
      {"type": "text", "text": "describe this image"},
      {"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": "data:image/png;base64,bm90IGFuIGltYWdl"}}
    ]}]
  }'
# Expected: 400. Actual: 500.
```

title: [Bug] DFLASH/DSPARK draft KV pool budget uses `tp_size` instead of `attn_tp_size`, causing OOM under DP attention in Kimi-K3
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

With DP attention enabled, the target KV pool consumes essentially the whole
`--mem-fraction-static` budget, and the draft worker OOMs when it allocates its
own KV pool afterwards.

The reservation for the DFLASH/DSPARK draft pool is computed from the *raw*
`tp_size`, while the draft pool is actually allocated sharded by `attn_tp_size`.
Under DP attention these differ by `attn_dp_size`, so the reservation is
under-counted by up to that factor.

### Failure chain

  1. `spec_aux_hidden_state._resolve_dflash_draft_cell_size` computes the draft
     pool's per-token cost and stores it as
     `SpecAuxHiddenStateConfig.dflash_draft_cell_size_per_token`.
  2. That config reaches the pool configurator as `spec_aux_config`.
     `DefaultPoolConfigurator.__init__` reads it via `_dflash_draft_cell_size()`
     and folds it into the per-token cell size:
     `_cell_size = target_cell_size_per_token + draft_cell_size_per_token`
     (`dflash_utils.scale_kv_cell_size_per_token_for_dflash`).
     `HybridSWAPoolConfigurator` reads the same field.
  3. `calculate_pool_sizes` turns that into the pool size:
     `max_total_num_tokens = available_bytes // _cell_size`.
  4. The draft term is computed from the raw `tp_size`, but every KV pool builder
     shards by `attn_tp_size`. With `--tp-size 16 --dp-size 16
     --enable-dp-attention`, `attn_tp_size` is `16 // 16 // 1 = 1` while the
     reservation still divides the draft's KV heads by 16.
  5. `_cell_size` therefore comes out too small, and `max_total_num_tokens` too
     large. Only the draft term is affected, so the inflation factor is
     `(target_cell + draft_cell) / (target_cell + draft_cell / attn_dp_size)`,
     not `attn_dp_size` itself.
  6. Both pools are then built at that inflated token count. The target pool stays
     within the budget — its own per-token cost was counted correctly. The draft
     pool does not: it allocates `max_total_num_tokens * draft_cell`, of which only
     `1 / attn_dp_size` was ever budgeted. The remaining `(attn_dp_size - 1) /
     attn_dp_size` is taken from the `(1 - mem_fraction_static)` runtime slack.
  7. When that slack is larger than the shortfall, startup succeeds and the
     overrun is invisible. When it is not, the draft worker OOMs while creating
     its KV buffers.

### Reproduction

Decode node of a PD deployment, Kimi-K3 target + DSPARK draft:

```
--tp-size 16 --dp-size 16 --ep-size 16
--enable-dp-attention --enable-dp-lm-head
--mamba-radix-cache-strategy extra_buffer_lazy
--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3
--mamba-ssm-dtype bfloat16
--disable-radix-cache
--enable-linear-replayssm-spec
--speculative-algorithm DSPARK
--speculative-draft-model-path $draft_model_path
--speculative-dspark-block-size 7
--mem-fraction-static 0.90
--disaggregation-mode decode
```

The failure lands in the draft worker's pool allocation:

```
scheduler.init_memory_pools
  -> draft_worker.alloc_memory_pool
    -> KVCacheConfigurator.configure
      -> _build_token_to_kv_pool -> _build_mha_kv_pool
        -> torch.OutOfMemoryError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 3.50 GiB.
           GPU has a total capacity of 267.69 GiB of which 1.46 GiB is free.
```

```
[rank1]:[W906 07:46:05.008634648 CUDACachingAllocator.cpp:3933] memory allocation failed with OOM on device 1 while trying to allocate 4334813184 bytes (free: 3779919872, total: 287431131136).
2026-09-06 15:46:07  if-ddjbovhieqyjamak-child-z25ds-worker-0  
[rank1]:[W906 07:46:05.009111435 CUDACachingAllocator.cpp:3933] memory allocation failed with OOM on device 1 while trying to allocate 4334813184 bytes (free: 3779919872, total: 287431131136).
2026-09-06 15:46:07  if-ddjbovhieqyjamak-child-z25ds-worker-0  
[2026-09-06 07:46:05 DP1 TP1 EP1] Scheduler hit an exception: Traceback (most recent call last):
2026-09-06 15:46:07  if-ddjbovhieqyjamak-child-z25ds-worker-0  
  File "/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py", line 5156, in run_scheduler_process
2026-09-06 15:46:07  if-ddjbovhieqyjamak-child-z25ds-worker-0  
    scheduler = Scheduler(
```
